    98→def _find_function_start(line: str, next_lines: list[str]) -> str | None:
    99→    """Return function name for declarations/assignments, else None."""
   100→    stripped = line.strip()
   101→    if not stripped:
   102→        return None
   103→    if stripped.startswith(("interface ", "type ", "enum ", "class ")):
   104→        return None
   105→
   106→    declaration_match = re.match(
   107→        r"^(?:export\s+)?(?:default\s+)?(?:async\s+)?function\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(",
   108→        stripped,
   109→    )
   110→    if declaration_match:
   111→        return declaration_match.group(1)
   112→
   113→    assignment_match = re.match(
   114→        r"^(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\b",
   115→        stripped,
   116→    )
   117→    if not assignment_match:
   118→        return None
   119→
   120→    combined = "\n".join(
   121→        [stripped] + [next_line.strip() for next_line in next_lines[:2]]
   122→    )
   123→    eq_pos = combined.find("=", assignment_match.end())
   124→    if eq_pos == -1:
   125→        return None
   126→    after_eq = combined[eq_pos + 1 :].lstrip()
   127→    if re.match(r"(?:async\s+)?\([^)]*\)\s*=>", after_eq):
   128→        return assignment_match.group(1)
   129→    if re.match(r"function\b", after_eq):
   130→        return assignment_match.group(1)
   131→    return None
   132→
   133→
   134→def _find_opening_brace_line(lines: list[str], start: int, *, window: int = 5) -> int | None:
   135→    for idx in range(start, min(start + window, len(lines))):
   136→        if "{" in lines[idx]:
   137→            return idx
   138→    return None
   139→
   140→
   141→def _extract_function_body(
   142→    lines: list[str], start_line: int, *, max_scan: int = 2000,
   143→) -> str | None:
   144→    """Extract the inner body text of a function starting at start_line.
   145→
   146→    Returns the text between the opening and closing braces, or None.
   147→    """
   148→    brace_line = _find_opening_brace_line(lines, start_line, window=5)
   149→    if brace_line is None:
   150→        return None
   151→    end_line = _track_brace_body(lines, brace_line, max_scan=max_scan)
   152→    if end_line is None:
   153→        return None
   154→    body_text = "\n".join(lines[brace_line : end_line + 1])
   155→    first_brace = body_text.find("{")
   156→    last_brace = body_text.rfind("}")
   157→    if first_brace == -1 or last_brace == -1 or first_brace >= last_brace:
   158→        return None
   159→    return body_text[first_brace + 1 : last_brace]
   160→
   161→
   162→def _count_pattern_in_body(body: str, pattern: re.Pattern[str]) -> int:
   163→    """Count regex matches in body that aren't inside string literals."""
   164→    return len(pattern.findall(_code_text(body)))
   165→
   166→
   167→def _compute_ts_cyclomatic_complexity(body: str) -> int:
   168→    """Compute cyclomatic complexity for a TypeScript function body string."""
   169→    stripped = _strip_ts_comments(body)
   170→    complexity = 1
   171→    for pattern in _TS_BRANCH_PATTERNS:
   172→        complexity += len(pattern.findall(stripped))
   173→    complexity += len(_OPERATOR_BRANCH_RE.findall(stripped))
   174→    return complexity
   175→
   176→
   177→# ── Detectors (alphabetical — uniform signature: ctx, smell_counts) ──
   178→
   179→
   180→def _detect_async_no_await(
   181→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   182→):
   183→    """Find async functions that don't use await."""
   184→    async_re = re.compile(r"(?:async\s+function\s+(\w+)|(\w+)\s*=\s*async)")
   185→    for i, line in enumerate(ctx.lines):
   186→        m = async_re.search(line)
   187→        if not m:
   188→            continue
   189→        name = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
   190→        body = _extract_function_body(ctx.lines, i)
   191→        if body is not None and not re.search(r"\bawait\b", _code_text(body)):
   192→            _emit(
   193→                smell_counts, "async_no_await", ctx, i + 1,
   194→                f"async {name or '(anonymous)'} has no await",
   195→            )
   196→
   197→
   198→def _detect_catch_return_default(
   199→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   200→):
   201→    """Find catch blocks that return object literals with default/no-op values.
   202→
   203→    Catches the pattern:
   204→      catch (...) { ... return { key: false, key: null, key: () => {} }; }
   205→
   206→    This is a silent failure — the caller gets valid-looking data but the
   207→    operation actually failed.
   208→    """
   209→    catch_re = re.compile(r"catch\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{")
   210→    for m in catch_re.finditer(ctx.content):
   211→        body = _extract_block_body(ctx.content, m.end() - 1, _MAX_CATCH_BODY)
   212→        if body is None:
   213→            continue
   214→
   215→        # Check if body contains "return {" — a return with object literal
   216→        return_obj = re.search(r"\breturn\s*\{", body)
   217→        if not return_obj:
   218→            continue
   219→
   220→        # Extract the returned object content
   221→        obj_start = body.find("{", return_obj.start())
   222→        obj_content = _extract_block_body(body, obj_start)
   223→        if obj_content is None:
   224→            continue
   225→
   226→        # Count default/no-op fields
   227→        noop_count = len(re.findall(r"\(\)\s*=>\s*\{\s*\}", obj_content))  # () => {}
   228→        false_count = len(
   229→            re.findall(r":\s*(?:false|null|undefined|0|''|\"\")\b", obj_content)
   230→        )
   231→        default_fields = noop_count + false_count
   232→
   233→        if default_fields >= _CATCH_DEFAULT_FIELD_THRESHOLD:
   234→            line_no, snippet = _content_line_info(ctx.content, m.start())
   235→            _emit(smell_counts, "catch_return_default", ctx, line_no, snippet)
   236→
   237→
   238→def _detect_dead_useeffects(
   239→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   240→) -> None:
   241→    """Find useEffect calls with empty/whitespace/comment-only bodies."""
   242→    for line_no, line in enumerate(ctx.lines):
   243→        stripped = line.strip()
   244→        if not re.match(r"(?:React\.)?useEffect\s*\(\s*\(\s*\)\s*=>\s*\{", stripped):
   245→            continue
   246→
   247→        text = "\n".join(ctx.lines[line_no : line_no + 30])
   248→        arrow_pos = text.find("=>")
   249→        if arrow_pos == -1:
   250→            continue
   251→        brace_pos = text.find("{", arrow_pos)
   252→        if brace_pos == -1:
   253→            continue
   254→
   255→        body = _extract_block_body(text, brace_pos)
   256→        if body is None:
   257→            continue
   258→
   259→        if _strip_ts_comments(body).strip() == "":
   260→            _emit(smell_counts, "dead_useeffect", ctx, line_no + 1, stripped[:100])
   261→
   262→
   263→def _scan_single_line_chain(
   264→    ctx: _FileContext, index: int, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   265→) -> int:
   266→    """Consume a single-line empty if/else-if chain starting at *index*. Returns next index."""
   267→    cursor = index + 1
   268→    while cursor < len(ctx.lines):
   269→        next_stripped = ctx.lines[cursor].strip()
   270→        if _SINGLE_EMPTY_ELSE_IF.match(next_stripped):
   271→            cursor += 1
   272→            continue
   273→        if _SINGLE_EMPTY_ELSE.match(next_stripped):
   274→            cursor += 1
   275→            continue
   276→        break
   277→    _emit(smell_counts, "empty_if_chain", ctx, index + 1, ctx.lines[index].strip()[:100])
   278→    return cursor
   279→
   280→
   281→def _scan_multi_line_chain(
   282→    ctx: _FileContext, index: int, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   283→) -> int:
   284→    """Consume a multi-line empty if/else chain starting at *index*. Returns next index."""
   285→    chain_all_empty = True
   286→    cursor = index
   287→    while cursor < len(ctx.lines):
   288→        current = ctx.lines[cursor].strip()
   289→        if cursor == index:
   290→            if not _MULTI_IF_OPEN.match(current):
   291→                chain_all_empty = False
   292→                break
   293→        elif _MULTI_ELSE_IF_OPEN.match(current):
   294→            pass
   295→        elif _MULTI_ELSE_OPEN.match(current):
   296→            pass
   297→        elif current == "}":
   298→            tail = cursor + 1
   299→            while tail < len(ctx.lines) and ctx.lines[tail].strip() == "":
   300→                tail += 1
   301→            if tail < len(ctx.lines) and _ELSE_CONT.match(ctx.lines[tail].strip()):
   302→                cursor = tail
   303→                continue
   304→            cursor += 1
   305→            break
   306→        elif current == "":
   307→            cursor += 1
   308→            continue
   309→        else:
   310→            chain_all_empty = False
   311→            break
   312→        cursor += 1
   313→    if chain_all_empty and cursor > index + 1:
   314→        _emit(smell_counts, "empty_if_chain", ctx, index + 1, ctx.lines[index].strip()[:100])
   315→    return max(index + 1, cursor)
   316→
   317→
   318→def _detect_empty_if_chains(
   319→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   320→) -> None:
   321→    """Find if/else chains where all branches are empty."""
   322→    index = 0
   323→    while index < len(ctx.lines):
   324→        stripped = ctx.lines[index].strip()
   325→        if not _IF_START.match(stripped):
   326→            index += 1
   327→            continue
   328→        if _SINGLE_EMPTY_IF.match(stripped):
   329→            index = _scan_single_line_chain(ctx, index, smell_counts)
   330→            continue
   331→        if _MULTI_IF_OPEN.match(stripped):
   332→            index = _scan_multi_line_chain(ctx, index, smell_counts)
   333→            continue
   334→        index += 1
   335→
   336→
   337→def _detect_error_no_throw(
   338→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   339→) -> None:
   340→    """Find console.error calls not followed by throw/return or other handling."""
   341→    # Skip files that are themselves logger/error-handler utilities.
   342→    basename = os.path.basename(ctx.filepath).lower()
   343→    basename_no_ext = os.path.splitext(basename)[0]
   344→    if any(tag in basename_no_ext for tag in _ERROR_HANDLER_BASENAMES):
   345→        return
   346→
   347→    for index, line in enumerate(ctx.lines):
   348→        if "console.error" not in line:
   349→            continue
   350→
   351→        # Skip if preceding 10 lines contain error-boundary or dev-only context.
   352→        preceding = "\n".join(ctx.lines[max(0, index - 10) : index])
   353→        if _PRECEDING_SKIP_PATTERNS.search(preceding):
   354→            continue
   355→
   356→        following = "\n".join(ctx.lines[index + 1 : index + 4])
   357→        if not _HANDLED_RE.search(following):
   358→            _emit(smell_counts, "console_error_no_throw", ctx, index + 1, line.strip()[:100])
   359→
   360→
   361→def _detect_high_cyclomatic_complexity(
   362→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   363→):
   364→    """Flag functions with cyclomatic complexity > 15."""
   365→    for i, line in enumerate(ctx.lines):
   366→        name = _find_function_start(line, ctx.lines[i + 1 : i + 3])
   367→        if not name:
   368→            continue
   369→
   370→        body = _extract_function_body(ctx.lines, i)
   371→        if body is None:
   372→            continue
   373→
   374→        complexity = _compute_ts_cyclomatic_complexity(body)
   375→        if complexity > _HIGH_CYCLOMATIC_THRESHOLD:
   376→            _emit(
   377→                smell_counts, "high_cyclomatic_complexity", ctx, i + 1,
   378→                f"{name}() — cyclomatic complexity {complexity}",
   379→            )
   380→
   381→
   382→def _detect_monster_functions(
   383→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   384→):
   385→    """Find functions/components exceeding 150 LOC via brace-tracking.
   386→
   387→    Matches: function declarations, named arrow functions, and React components.
   388→    Skips: interfaces, types, enums, and objects/arrays.
   389→    """
   390→    for i, line in enumerate(ctx.lines):
   391→        name = _find_function_start(line, ctx.lines[i + 1 : i + 3])
   392→        if not name:
   393→            continue
   394→
   395→        brace_line = _find_opening_brace_line(ctx.lines, i, window=5)
   396→        if brace_line is None:
   397→            continue
   398→
   399→        end_line = _track_brace_body(ctx.lines, brace_line, max_scan=2000)
   400→        if end_line is not None:
   401→            loc = end_line - i + 1
   402→            if loc > _MONSTER_FUNCTION_LOC:
   403→                _emit(
   404→                    smell_counts, "monster_function", ctx, i + 1,
   405→                    f"{name}() — {loc} LOC",
   406→                )
   407→
   408→
   409→def _detect_nested_closures(
   410→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   411→):
   412→    """Find functions with >= 3 nested closure definitions."""
   413→    for i, line in enumerate(ctx.lines):
   414→        name = _find_function_start(line, ctx.lines[i + 1 : i + 3])
   415→        if not name:
   416→            continue
   417→
   418→        body = _extract_function_body(ctx.lines, i)
   419→        if body is None:
   420→            continue
   421→
   422→        closure_count = (
   423→            _count_pattern_in_body(body, _FUNC_RE)
   424→            + _count_pattern_in_body(body, _ARROW_RE)
   425→        )
   426→        if closure_count >= _NESTED_CLOSURE_THRESHOLD:
   427→            _emit(
   428→                smell_counts, "nested_closure", ctx, i + 1,
   429→                f"{name}() — {closure_count} nested closures",
   430→            )
   431→
   432→
   433→def _detect_stub_functions(
   434→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   435→):
   436→    """Find functions with empty body or only return/return null (stub functions).
   437→
   438→    Matches function declarations and named arrow functions.
   439→    Skips decorated functions (TS decorators on line above).
   440→    """
   441→    for i, line in enumerate(ctx.lines):
   442→        if i > 0 and ctx.lines[i - 1].strip().startswith("@"):
   443→            continue
   444→
   445→        name = _find_function_start(line, ctx.lines[i + 1 : i + 3])
   446→        if not name:
   447→            continue
   448→
   449→        body = _extract_function_body(ctx.lines, i, max_scan=30)
   450→        if body is None:
   451→            continue
   452→
   453→        body_clean = _strip_ts_comments(body).strip().rstrip(";")
   454→        if body_clean in ("", "return", "return null", "return undefined"):
   455→            label = body_clean or "empty"
   456→            _emit(
   457→                smell_counts, "stub_function", ctx, i + 1,
   458→                f"{name}() — body is {label}",
   459→            )
   460→
   461→
   462→def _detect_swallowed_errors(
   463→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   464→) -> None:
   465→    """Find catch blocks whose only content is console.error/warn/log."""
   466→    catch_re = re.compile(r"catch\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{")
   467→    for match in catch_re.finditer(ctx.content):
   468→        body = _extract_block_body(ctx.content, match.end() - 1, 500)
   469→        if body is None:
   470→            continue
   471→
   472→        body_clean = _strip_ts_comments(body).strip()
   473→        if not body_clean:
   474→            continue
   475→
   476→        statements = [
   477→            stmt.strip().rstrip(";")
   478→            for stmt in re.split(r"[;\n]", body_clean)
   479→            if stmt.strip()
   480→        ]
   481→        if not statements:
   482→            continue
   483→
   484→        all_console = all(
   485→            re.match(r"console\.(error|warn|log)\s*\(", stmt) for stmt in statements
   486→        )
   487→        if all_console:
   488→            line_no, snippet = _content_line_info(ctx.content, match.start())
   489→            _emit(smell_counts, "swallowed_error", ctx, line_no, snippet)
   490→
   491→
   492→def _detect_switch_no_default(
   493→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   494→):
   495→    """Flag switch statements that have no default case."""
   496→    switch_re = re.compile(r"\bswitch\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\{")
   497→    for m in switch_re.finditer(ctx.content):
   498→        body = _extract_block_body(ctx.content, m.end() - 1, _MAX_SWITCH_BODY_SCAN)
   499→        if body is None:
   500→            continue
   501→
   502→        # Count case labels — only flag if there are actual cases
   503→        case_count = len(re.findall(r"\bcase\s+", body))
   504→        if case_count < _SWITCH_CASE_MINIMUM:
   505→            continue
   506→
   507→        if re.search(r"\bdefault\s*:", body):
   508→            continue
   509→
   510→        line_no, snippet = _content_line_info(ctx.content, m.start())
   511→        _emit(smell_counts, "switch_no_default", ctx, line_no, snippet)
   512→
   513→
   514→def _detect_window_globals(
   515→    ctx: _FileContext, smell_counts: dict[str, list[dict]]
   516→):
   517→    """Find window.__* assignments — global state escape hatches.
   518→
   519→    Matches:
   520→    - window.__foo = ...
   521→    - (window as any).__foo = ...
   522→    - window['__foo'] = ...
   523→    """
   524→    window_re = re.compile(
   525→        r"""(?:"""
   526→        r"""\(?\s*window\s+as\s+any\s*\)?\s*\.\s*(?:__\w+)"""  # (window as any).__name
   527→        r"""|window\s*\.\s*(?:__\w+)"""  # window.__name
   528→        r"""|window\s*\[\s*['"](?:__\w+)['"]\s*\]"""  # window['__name']
   529→        r""")\s*=""",
   530→    )
   531→    for i, line in enumerate(ctx.lines):
   532→        if i in ctx.line_state:
   533→            continue
   534→        m = window_re.search(line)
   535→        if not m:
   536→            continue
   537→        if _ts_match_is_in_string(line, m.start()):
   538→            continue
   539→        _emit(smell_counts, "window_global", ctx, i + 1, line.strip()[:100])
   540→

1→"""Reusable CLI rendering snippets for command modules."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections.abc import Callable
     6→
     7→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.queue_progress import (
     8→    QueueBreakdown,

    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import rel
    12→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
    13→
    14→
    15→def print_agent_plan(
    16→    steps: list[str],
    17→    *,
    18→    next_command: str | None = None,
    19→    header: str = "  AGENT PLAN:",
    20→    plan: dict | None = None,
    21→) -> None:
    22→    """Print a consistent AGENT PLAN block with numbered steps.
    23→
    24→    When a living *plan* is active, renders plan focus/progress instead
    25→    of the narrative-derived steps.
    26→    """
    27→    if plan and (plan.get("queue_order") or plan.get("clusters")):
    28→        _print_plan_agent_block(plan, header=header)
    29→        return
    30→    if not steps:
    31→        return
    32→    print(colorize(header, "yellow"))
    33→    for idx, step in enumerate(steps, 1):
    34→        print(colorize(f"  {idx}. {step}", "dim"))
    35→    if next_command:
    36→        print(colorize(f"  Next command: `{next_command}`", "dim"))
    37→
    38→
    39→def _print_plan_agent_block(plan: dict, *, header: str = "  AGENT PLAN:") -> None:
    40→    """Render the living plan as the agent plan block."""
    41→    active = plan.get("active_cluster")
    42→    ordered = len(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    43→    skipped_ids = set(plan.get("skipped", {}).keys())
    44→    skipped = len(skipped_ids)
    45→    queue_order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    46→    plan_ordered = sum(1 for fid in queue_order if fid not in skipped_ids)
    47→
    48→    # Build a lightweight breakdown for the headline
    49→    breakdown = QueueBreakdown(
    50→        queue_total=ordered,
    51→        plan_ordered=plan_ordered,
    52→        skipped=skipped,
    53→    )
    54→    headline = format_queue_headline(breakdown)
    55→
    56→    print(colorize(header, "yellow"))
    57→    print(colorize(f"  Living plan active: {headline}", "dim"))
    58→    if active:
    59→        cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(active, {})
    60→        remaining = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    61→        print(colorize(f"  Focused on: {active} ({remaining} items remaining).", "dim"))
    62→    print(colorize("  Next command: `desloppify next`", "dim"))
    63→    print(colorize("  View plan: `desloppify plan`", "dim"))
    64→
    65→
    66→def print_replacement_groups(
    67→    groups: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]],
    68→    *,
    69→    title: str,
    70→    rel_fn: Callable[[str], str] = rel,
    71→) -> None:
    72→    """Print grouped old→new replacement lines by file."""
    73→    if not groups:
    74→        return
    75→    print(colorize(title, "cyan"))
    76→    for filepath, replacements in sorted(groups.items()):
    77→        print(f"    {rel_fn(filepath)}:")
    78→        for old, new in replacements:
    79→            print(f"      {old}  →  {new}")
    80→    print()
    81→
    82→
    83→def print_ranked_actions(
    84→    actions: list[dict], *, limit: int = 3, plan: dict | None = None
    85→) -> bool:
    86→    """Print the highest-impact narrative actions and return True when shown."""
    87→    ranked = sorted(
    88→        [action for action in actions if int(action.get("count", 0)) > 0],
    89→        key=lambda action: (
    90→            -float(action.get("impact", 0.0)),
    91→            -int(action.get("count", 0)),
    92→            int(action.get("priority", 999)),
    93→        ),
    94→    )
    95→    if not ranked:
    96→        return False
    97→    has_plan = plan and (plan.get("queue_order") or plan.get("clusters"))
    98→    label = "Score context:" if has_plan else "Biggest things impacting score:"
    99→    print(colorize(f"  {label}", "cyan"))
   100→    for action in ranked[:limit]:
   101→        detector = action.get("detector", "unknown")
   102→        count = int(action.get("count", 0))
   103→        cluster_count = action.get("cluster_count")
   104→        if cluster_count:
   105→            print(colorize(f"    - {detector}: {count} open in {cluster_count} cluster(s) — `desloppify next`", "dim"))
   106→        else:
   107→            command = action.get("command", "desloppify next")
   108→            print(colorize(f"    - {detector}: {count} open — `{command}`", "dim"))
   109→    return True
   110→
   111→
   112→__all__ = [
   113→    "print_agent_plan",
   114→    "print_ranked_actions",
   115→    "print_replacement_groups",
   116→]

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations

     5→import logging
     6→from pathlib import Path

     8→from desloppify import languages as lang_api
     9→from desloppify import state as state_mod

    20→def audit_excluded_dirs(
    21→    exclusions: tuple[str, ...],
    22→    scanned_files: list[str],
    23→    project_root: Path,
    24→) -> list[dict]:
    25→    """Check if any --exclude directory has zero references from scanned code.
    26→
    27→    Returns issues for directories that appear stale (no file references them).
    28→    """
    29→    if not exclusions:
    30→        return []
    31→
    32→    candidate_dirs = [
    33→        ex_dir
    34→        for ex_dir in exclusions
    35→        if ex_dir not in DEFAULT_EXCLUSIONS and (project_root / ex_dir).is_dir()
    36→    ]
    37→    if not candidate_dirs:
    38→        return []
    39→
    40→    # Read each scanned file once and mark any exclusions observed in content.
    41→    unresolved = set(candidate_dirs)
    42→    for filepath in scanned_files:
    43→        if not unresolved:
    44→            break
    45→        abs_path = (
    46→            filepath if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else str(project_root / filepath)
    47→        )
    48→        content = read_file_text(abs_path)
    49→        if content is None:
    50→            logger.debug(
    51→                "Skipping unreadable file %s while auditing exclusions", filepath
    52→            )
    53→            continue
    54→
    55→        matched = {ex_dir for ex_dir in unresolved if ex_dir in content}
    56→        if matched:
    57→            unresolved.difference_update(matched)
    58→
    59→    stale_issues = []
    60→    for ex_dir in candidate_dirs:
    61→        if ex_dir not in unresolved:
    62→            continue
    63→        stale_issues.append(
    64→            state_mod.make_issue(
    65→                "stale_exclude",
    66→                ex_dir,
    67→                ex_dir,
    68→                tier=4,
    69→                confidence="low",
    70→                summary=(
    71→                    f"Excluded directory '{ex_dir}' has 0 references from scanned code — "
    72→                    "may be stale"
    73→                ),
    74→                detail={"directory": ex_dir, "references": 0},
    75→            )
    76→        )
    77→    return stale_issues

    80→def collect_codebase_metrics(lang, path: Path) -> dict | None:

    82→    if not lang or not lang.file_finder:

    84→    files = lang.file_finder(path)
    85→    total_loc = 0
    86→    dirs = set()
    87→    for filepath in files:
    88→        try:
    89→            total_loc += count_lines(Path(filepath))
    90→            dirs.add(str(Path(filepath).parent))
    91→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
    92→            logger.debug(
    93→                "Skipping unreadable file %s while collecting scan metrics: %s",
    94→                filepath,
    95→                exc,
    96→            )
    97→    return {
    98→        "total_files": len(files),
    99→        "total_loc": total_loc,
   100→        "total_directories": len(dirs),
   101→    }
   102→
   103→
   104→def resolve_scan_profile(profile: str | None, lang) -> str:
   105→    """Resolve effective scan profile from CLI and language defaults."""
   106→    if profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:
   107→        return profile
   108→    default_profile = getattr(lang, "default_scan_profile", "full") if lang else "full"
   109→    if default_profile in {"objective", "full", "ci"}:
   110→        return default_profile
   111→    return "full"
   112→
   113→
   114→def effective_include_slow(include_slow: bool, profile: str) -> bool:
   115→    """Determine whether slow phases should run for this profile."""
   116→    return include_slow and profile != "ci"
   117→
   118→
   119→def _format_hidden_by_detector(hidden_by_detector: dict[str, int]) -> str:
   120→    """Format hidden issues counts for terminal output."""
   121→    return ", ".join(f"{det}: +{count}" for det, count in hidden_by_detector.items())
   122→
   123→
   124→def warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files(
   125→    args, lang, path: Path, metrics: dict | None
   126→) -> None:
   127→    """Warn when user explicitly selected a language but scan found zero files."""
   128→    explicit_lang = getattr(args, "lang", None)
   129→    if not explicit_lang or not lang or not metrics:
   130→        return
   131→    if metrics.get("total_files", 0) > 0:
   132→        return
   133→
   134→    suggestion = " Omit `--lang` to auto-detect."
   135→    root = path if path.is_dir() else path.parent
   136→    try:
   137→        detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(root)
   138→    except ValueError as exc:
   139→        detected = None
   140→        logger.debug(
   141→            "Auto-detect failed while warning for explicit lang on %s: %s", root, exc
   142→        )
   143→    else:
   144→        if detected and detected != lang.name:
   145→            suggestion = (
   146→                f" Detected `{detected}` for this path — use `--lang {detected}` "
   147→                "or omit `--lang`."
   148→            )
   149→
   150→    print(
   151→        colorize(
   152→            f"  ⚠ No {lang.name} source files found under `{path}`.{suggestion}",
   153→            "yellow",
   154→        )
   155→    )
   156→
   157→
   158→def format_delta(value: float, prev: float | None) -> tuple[str, str]:
   159→    """Return (delta_str, color) for a score change."""
   160→    delta = value - prev if prev is not None else 0
   161→    delta_str = f" ({'+' if delta > 0 else ''}{delta:.1f})" if delta != 0 else ""
   162→    color = "green" if delta > 0 else ("red" if delta < 0 else "dim")
   163→    return delta_str, color
   164→
   165→
   166→__all__ = [

   171→    "_format_hidden_by_detector",
   172→    "resolve_scan_profile",
   173→    "warn_explicit_lang_with_no_files",

    46→def _ts_match_is_in_string(line: str, match_start: int) -> bool:
    47→    """Check if a match position falls inside a string literal or comment on a single line.
    48→
    49→    Mirrors Python's _match_is_in_string but for TS syntax (', ", `, //).
    50→    """
    51→    i = 0
    52→    in_str = None
    53→
    54→    while i < len(line):
    55→        if i == match_start:
    56→            return in_str is not None
    57→
    58→        ch = line[i]
    59→
    60→        # Escape sequences inside strings
    61→        if in_str and ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(line):
    62→            i += 2
    63→            continue
    64→
    65→        if in_str:
    66→            if ch == in_str:
    67→                in_str = None
    68→            i += 1
    69→            continue
    70→
    71→        # Line comment — everything after is non-code
    72→        if ch == "/" and i + 1 < len(line) and line[i + 1] == "/":
    73→            return match_start > i
    74→
    75→        if ch in ("'", '"', "`"):
    76→            in_str = ch
    77→            i += 1
    78→            continue

    80→        i += 1
    81→
    82→    return False

    85→def _track_brace_body(
    86→    lines: list[str], start_line: int, *, max_scan: int = 2000
    87→) -> int | None:
    88→    """Find the closing brace that matches the first opening brace from start_line.
    89→
    90→    Tracks brace depth with string-literal awareness (', ", `).
    91→    Returns the line index of the closing brace, or None if not found.
    92→    """
    93→    depth = 0
    94→    found_open = False
    95→    for line_idx in range(start_line, min(start_line + max_scan, len(lines))):
    96→        for _, ch, in_string in scan_code(lines[line_idx]):
    97→            if in_string:
    98→                continue
    99→            if ch == "{":
   100→                depth += 1
   101→                found_open = True
   102→            elif ch == "}":
   103→                depth -= 1
   104→                if found_open and depth == 0:
   105→                    return line_idx
   106→    return None
   107→
   108→
   109→def _find_block_end(content: str, brace_start: int, max_scan: int = 5000) -> int | None:
   110→    """Find the closing brace position in a content string starting from an opening brace.
   111→
   112→    Uses scan_code for string-literal awareness. Returns the index of the
   113→    matching ``}`` or None.
   114→    """
   115→    depth = 0
   116→    for ci, ch, in_s in scan_code(
   117→        content, brace_start, min(brace_start + max_scan, len(content))
   118→    ):
   119→        if in_s:
   120→            continue
   121→        if ch == "{":
   122→            depth += 1
   123→        elif ch == "}":
   124→            depth -= 1
   125→            if depth == 0:
   126→                return ci
   127→    return None
   128→
   129→
   130→def _extract_block_body(
   131→    content: str, brace_start: int, max_scan: int = 5000
   132→) -> str | None:
   133→    """Return the text between ``{`` at *brace_start* and its matching ``}``.
   134→
   135→    Delegates to :func:`_find_block_end` for brace tracking.
   136→    Returns ``None`` when the closing brace is not found.
   137→    """
   138→    end = _find_block_end(content, brace_start, max_scan)
   139→    if end is None:
   140→        return None
   141→    return content[brace_start + 1 : end]
   142→
   143→
   144→def _content_line_info(content: str, pos: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
   145→    """Return ``(1-based line number, stripped snippet[:100])`` for a position in *content*."""
   146→    line_no = content[:pos].count("\n") + 1
   147→    line_start = content.rfind("\n", 0, pos) + 1
   148→    line_end = content.find("\n", pos)
   149→    if line_end == -1:
   150→        line_end = len(content)
   151→    return line_no, content[line_start:line_end].strip()[:100]
   152→
   153→
   154→def _code_text(text: str) -> str:
   155→    """Blank string literals and ``//`` comments to spaces, preserving positions.
   156→
   157→    Built on :func:`scan_code` with added line-comment detection.
   158→    """
   159→    out = list(text)
   160→    in_line_comment = False
   161→    prev_code_idx = -2
   162→    prev_code_ch = ""
   163→    for i, ch, in_s in scan_code(text):
   164→        if ch == "\n":
   165→            in_line_comment = False
   166→            prev_code_ch = ""
   167→            continue
   168→        if in_line_comment:
   169→            out[i] = " "
   170→            continue
   171→        if in_s:
   172→            out[i] = " "
   173→            continue
   174→        if ch == "/" and prev_code_ch == "/" and prev_code_idx == i - 1:
   175→            out[prev_code_idx] = " "
   176→            out[i] = " "
   177→            in_line_comment = True
   178→            prev_code_ch = ""
   179→            continue
   180→        prev_code_idx = i
   181→        prev_code_ch = ch
   182→    return "".join(out)
   183→
   184→
   185→def _scan_template_content(
   186→    line: str, start: int, brace_depth: int = 0
   187→) -> tuple[int, bool, int]:
   188→    """Scan template literal content from *start* in *line*.
   189→
   190→    Returns ``(end_pos, found_close, brace_depth)`` where *found_close* is True
   191→    if a closing backtick was found and *end_pos* is the position after it.
   192→    """
   193→    j = start
   194→    while j < len(line):
   195→        ch = line[j]
   196→        if ch == "\\" and j + 1 < len(line):
   197→            j += 2
   198→            continue
   199→        if ch == "$" and j + 1 < len(line) and line[j + 1] == "{":
   200→            brace_depth += 1
   201→            j += 2
   202→            continue
   203→        if ch == "}" and brace_depth > 0:
   204→            brace_depth -= 1
   205→            j += 1
   206→            continue
   207→        if ch == "`" and brace_depth == 0:
   208→            return (j + 1, True, brace_depth)
   209→        j += 1
   210→    return (j, False, brace_depth)
   211→
   212→
   213→def _scan_code_line(line: str) -> tuple[bool, bool, int]:
   214→    """Scan a normal code line for block comment or template literal start.
   215→
   216→    Returns ``(entered_block_comment, entered_template, template_brace_depth)``.
   217→    """
   218→    j = 0
   219→    in_str = None
   220→    while j < len(line):
   221→        ch = line[j]
   222→
   223→        # Skip escape sequences
   224→        if in_str and ch == "\\" and j + 1 < len(line):
   225→            j += 2
   226→            continue
   227→
   228→        # String tracking
   229→        if in_str:
   230→            if ch == in_str:
   231→                in_str = None
   232→            j += 1
   233→            continue
   234→
   235→        # Line comment — rest is not code
   236→        if ch == "/" and j + 1 < len(line) and line[j + 1] == "/":
   237→            break
   238→
   239→        # Block comment start
   240→        if ch == "/" and j + 1 < len(line) and line[j + 1] == "*":
   241→            # Check if it closes on same line
   242→            close = line.find("*/", j + 2)
   243→            if close != -1:
   244→                j = close + 2
   245→                continue
   246→            return (True, False, 0)
   247→
   248→        # Template literal start
   249→        if ch == "`":
   250→            end_pos, found_close, depth = _scan_template_content(line, j + 1)
   251→            if found_close:
   252→                j = end_pos
   253→                continue
   254→            return (False, True, depth)
   255→
   256→        if ch in ("'", '"'):
   257→            in_str = ch
   258→            j += 1
   259→            continue
   260→
   261→        j += 1
   262→
   263→    return (False, False, 0)
   264→
   265→
   266→def _build_ts_line_state(lines: list[str]) -> dict[int, str]:
   267→    """Build a map of line numbers that are inside block comments or template literals.
   268→
   269→    Returns {0-indexed line: reason} where reason is "block_comment" or "template_literal".
   270→    Lines not in the map are normal code lines suitable for regex checks.
   271→
   272→    Tracks:
   273→    - Block comment state (opened by /*, closed by */)
   274→    - Template literal state (opened by backtick, closed by backtick,
   275→      with ${} nesting awareness)
   276→    """
   277→    state: dict[int, str] = {}
   278→    in_block_comment = False
   279→    in_template = False
   280→    template_brace_depth = 0
   281→
   282→    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   283→        if in_block_comment:
   284→            state[i] = "block_comment"
   285→            if "*/" in line:
   286→                in_block_comment = False
   287→            continue
   288→
   289→        if in_template:
   290→            state[i] = "template_literal"
   291→            _, found_close, template_brace_depth = _scan_template_content(
   292→                line, 0, template_brace_depth
   293→            )
   294→            if found_close:
   295→                in_template = False
   296→            continue
   297→
   298→        in_block_comment, in_template, depth = _scan_code_line(line)
   299→        if in_template:
   300→            template_brace_depth = depth
   301→
   302→    return state

1→"""Helper utilities for plan triage workflow."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→from collections import defaultdict
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     9→from desloppify.engine.plan import (
    10→    TRIAGE_IDS,
    11→    TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS,
    12→    purge_ids,
    13→    review_issue_snapshot_hash,
    14→)
    15→from desloppify.state import utc_now
    16→
    17→from .services import TriageServices, default_triage_services
    18→
    19→_STAGE_ORDER = ["observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich"]
    20→
    21→
    22→def has_triage_in_queue(plan: dict) -> bool:
    23→    """Check if any triage stage ID is in the queue."""
    24→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    25→    return bool(order & TRIAGE_IDS)
    26→
    27→def inject_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> None:
    28→    """Inject all 4 triage stage IDs into the queue (fresh start)."""
    29→    order: list[str] = plan.setdefault("queue_order", [])
    30→    existing = set(order)
    31→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    32→        if sid not in existing:
    33→            order.insert(0 if sid == TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS[0] else len(order), sid)
    34→    # Re-insert in correct order at front
    35→    for sid in reversed(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS):
    36→        if sid in order:
    37→            order.remove(sid)
    38→    insert_at = 0
    39→    for sid in TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS:
    40→        order.insert(insert_at, sid)
    41→        insert_at += 1
    42→
    43→def purge_triage_stage(plan: dict, stage_name: str) -> None:
    44→    """Purge a single triage stage ID from the queue."""
    45→    sid = f"triage::{stage_name}"
    46→    purge_ids(plan, [sid])
    47→
    48→def cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages: dict, from_stage: str) -> list[str]:
    49→    """Clear confirmed_at/confirmed_text on stages AFTER *from_stage*. Returns cleared names."""
    50→    try:
    51→        idx = _STAGE_ORDER.index(from_stage)
    52→    except ValueError:
    53→        return []
    54→    cleared: list[str] = []
    55→    for later in _STAGE_ORDER[idx + 1:]:
    56→        if later in stages and stages[later].get("confirmed_at"):
    57→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_at", None)
    58→            stages[later].pop("confirmed_text", None)
    59→            cleared.append(later)
    60→    return cleared
    61→
    62→def print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared: list[str], stages: dict) -> None:
    63→    """Print yellow cascade-clear message with next-step guidance."""
    64→    if not cleared:
    65→        return
    66→    print(colorize(f"  Cleared confirmations on: {', '.join(cleared)}", "yellow"))
    67→    next_unconfirmed = next(
    68→        (s for s in _STAGE_ORDER if s in stages and not stages[s].get("confirmed_at")),
    69→        None,
    70→    )
    71→    if next_unconfirmed:
    72→        print(colorize(
    73→            f"  Re-confirm with: desloppify plan triage --confirm {next_unconfirmed}",
    74→            "dim",
    75→        ))
    76→
    77→def observe_dimension_breakdown(si) -> tuple[dict[str, int], list[str]]:
    78→    """Count issues per dimension from a TriageInput. Returns (by_dim, sorted_dim_names)."""
    79→    by_dim: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
    80→    for _fid, f in si.open_issues.items():
    81→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
    82→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
    83→        by_dim[dim] += 1
    84→    dim_names = sorted(by_dim, key=lambda d: (-by_dim[d], d))
    85→    return dict(by_dim), dim_names
    86→
    87→def open_review_ids_from_state(state: dict) -> set[str]:
    88→    """Return IDs of all open review/concerns issues in state."""
    89→    return {
    90→        fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
    91→        if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
    92→    }
    93→
    94→def triage_coverage(
    95→    plan: dict,
    96→    open_review_ids: set[str] | None = None,
    97→) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
    98→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for review issues in triage.
    99→
   100→    When *open_review_ids* is provided, use it as the full set of review
   101→    issues (from state) instead of falling back to queue_order.
   102→    """
   103→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   104→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
   105→    for c in clusters.values():
   106→        all_cluster_ids.update(c.get("issue_ids", []))
   107→    if open_review_ids is not None:
   108→        review_ids = list(open_review_ids)
   109→    else:
   110→        review_ids = [
   111→            fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   112→            if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::") and (fid.startswith("review::") or fid.startswith("concerns::"))
   113→        ]
   114→    organized = sum(1 for fid in review_ids if fid in all_cluster_ids)
   115→    return organized, len(review_ids), clusters
   116→
   117→def manual_clusters_with_issues(plan: dict) -> list[str]:
   118→    """Return names of non-auto clusters that have issues."""
   119→    return [
   120→        name for name, c in plan.get("clusters", {}).items()
   121→        if c.get("issue_ids") and not c.get("auto")
   122→    ]
   123→
   124→def apply_completion(
   125→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   126→    plan: dict,
   127→    strategy: str,
   128→    *,
   129→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   130→) -> None:
   131→    """Shared completion logic: update meta, remove triage::pending, save."""
   132→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   133→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   134→    state = runtime.state
   135→
   136→    organized, total, clusters = triage_coverage(
   137→        plan, open_review_ids=open_review_ids_from_state(state),
   138→    )
   139→
   140→    # Purge all triage stage IDs.
   141→    purge_ids(plan, list(TRIAGE_IDS))
   142→
   143→    current_hash = review_issue_snapshot_hash(state)
   144→
   145→    meta = plan.setdefault("epic_triage_meta", {})
   146→    meta["issue_snapshot_hash"] = current_hash
   147→    open_ids = sorted(
   148→        fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   149→        if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   150→    )
   151→    meta["triaged_ids"] = open_ids
   152→    if strategy.strip().lower() != "same":
   153→        meta["strategy_summary"] = strategy
   154→    meta["trigger"] = "manual_triage"
   155→    meta["last_completed_at"] = utc_now()
   156→    # Archive stages before clearing so previous analysis is preserved
   157→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   158→    if stages:
   159→        meta["last_triage"] = {
   160→            "completed_at": utc_now(),
   161→            "stages": {k: dict(v) for k, v in stages.items()},
   162→            "strategy": strategy if strategy.strip().lower() != "same" else meta.get("strategy_summary", ""),
   163→        }
   164→    meta["triage_stages"] = {}  # clear stages on completion
   165→    meta.pop("stage_refresh_required", None)
   166→    meta.pop("stage_snapshot_hash", None)
   167→
   168→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   169→
   170→    cluster_count = len([c for c in clusters.values() if c.get("issue_ids")])
   171→    print(colorize(f"  Triage complete: {organized}/{total} issues in {cluster_count} cluster(s).", "green"))
   172→    effective_strategy = strategy if strategy.strip().lower() != "same" else meta.get("strategy_summary", "")
   173→    if effective_strategy:
   174→        print(colorize(f"  Strategy: {effective_strategy}", "cyan"))
   175→    print(colorize("  Run `desloppify next` to start implementation.", "green"))
   176→
   177→def find_cluster_for(fid: str, clusters: dict) -> str | None:
   178→    """Return the cluster name containing *fid*, or None."""
   179→    for name, c in clusters.items():
   180→        if fid in c.get("issue_ids", []):
   181→            return name
   182→    return None
   183→
   184→def count_log_activity_since(plan: dict, since: str) -> dict[str, int]:
   185→    """Count execution log entries by action since *since* timestamp."""
   186→    counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   187→    for entry in plan.get("execution_log", []):
   188→        if entry.get("timestamp", "") >= since:
   189→            counts[entry.get("action", "unknown")] += 1
   190→    return dict(counts)

    37→def _suggest_close_matches(state: dict, plan: dict | None, patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    38→    """Print fuzzy match suggestions for patterns that resolved to zero issues."""
    39→    all_ids: list[str] = list(state.get("issues", {}).keys())
    40→    if plan is not None:
    41→        seen_ids: set[str] = set(all_ids)
    42→        for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    43→            if fid not in seen_ids:
    44→                seen_ids.add(fid)
    45→                all_ids.append(fid)
    46→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    47→            for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    48→                if fid not in seen_ids:
    49→                    seen_ids.add(fid)
    50→                    all_ids.append(fid)
    51→
    52→    for pattern in patterns:
    53→        segments = pattern.split("::")
    54→        last_seg = segments[-1]
    55→        suggestions: list[str] = []
    56→
    57→        if _HEX8_RE.match(last_seg):
    58→            suggestions = [fid for fid in all_ids if fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}") or fid == last_seg]
    59→            if suggestions:
    60→                print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    61→                print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    62→                for m in suggestions[:3]:
    63→                    print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    64→                print(colorize(f"  Tip: match by hash suffix alone: {last_seg}", "dim"))
    65→            continue
    66→
    67→        # Try last segment and second-to-last as descriptive name slugs
    68→        slug = segments[-2] if len(segments) >= 2 else ""
    69→        for fid in all_ids:
    70→            if f"::{last_seg}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}"):
    71→                suggestions.append(fid)
    72→            elif slug and (f"::{slug}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{slug}")):
    73→                suggestions.append(fid)
    74→        if suggestions:
    75→            print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    76→            print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    77→            for m in suggestions[:3]:
    78→                print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))

   232→def _resolve_item_position(
   233→    position: str,
   234→    target: str | None,
   235→    item_ids: list[str],
   236→    ordered_slice: list[str],
   237→    cluster_member_set: set[str],
   238→    cluster_name: str,
   239→    state: dict,
   240→    plan: dict,
   241→) -> tuple[str, str | None, int | None] | None:
   242→    """Resolve where items should be positioned within a cluster.
   243→
   244→    Returns (resolved_position, resolved_target, offset) on success,
   245→    or None if an error was printed and the caller should abort.
   246→    """
   247→    item_set = set(item_ids)
   248→
   249→    if position == "top":
   250→        first_non_item = next((fid for fid in ordered_slice if fid not in item_set), None)
   251→        if first_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[:len(item_ids)]) == item_set:
   252→            print(colorize("  Already at the top of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   253→            return None
   254→        return ("before", first_non_item, None)
   255→
   256→    if position == "bottom":
   257→        last_non_item = next((fid for fid in reversed(ordered_slice) if fid not in item_set), None)
   258→        if last_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[-len(item_ids):]) == item_set:
   259→            print(colorize("  Already at the bottom of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   260→            return None
   261→        return ("after", last_non_item, None)
   262→
   263→    if position in ("before", "after"):
   264→        if target is None:
   265→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires a target. Example: --item PAT {position} TARGET", "red"))
   266→            return None
   267→        target_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [target], plan=plan)
   268→        if not target_ids:
   269→            print(colorize(f"  No match for target {target!r}.", "yellow"))
   270→            return None
   271→        resolved_target = target_ids[0]
   272→        if resolved_target not in cluster_member_set:
   273→            print(colorize(f"  Target {resolved_target!r} is not in cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   274→            return None
   275→        return (position, resolved_target, None)
   276→
   277→    if position in ("up", "down"):
   278→        if target is None:
   279→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires an offset. Example: --item PAT {position} 3", "red"))
   280→            return None
   281→        try:
   282→            offset = int(target)
   283→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   284→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   285→            return None
   286→        return (position, None, offset)
   287→
   288→    return (position, None, None)
   289→
   290→
   291→def _reorder_within_cluster(
   292→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   293→    plan: dict,
   294→    clusters: dict,
   295→    cluster_names: list[str],
   296→    position: str,
   297→    target: str | None,
   298→    item_pattern: str,
   299→) -> None:
   300→    """Reorder items within a single cluster."""
   301→    if len(cluster_names) != 1:
   302→        print(colorize("  --item requires exactly one cluster name.", "red"))
   303→        return
   304→    cluster_name = cluster_names[0]
   305→    cluster_member_set = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids", []))
   306→
   307→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   308→    item_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [item_pattern], plan=plan)
   309→    if not item_ids:
   310→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found for --item pattern.", "yellow"))
   311→        return
   312→    for fid in item_ids:
   313→        if fid not in cluster_member_set:
   314→            print(colorize(f"  {fid!r} is not a member of cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   315→            return
   316→
   317→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   318→    ordered_slice = [fid for fid in queue_order if fid in cluster_member_set]
   319→
   320→    result = _resolve_item_position(
   321→        position, target, item_ids, ordered_slice,
   322→        cluster_member_set, cluster_name, state, plan,
   323→    )
   324→    if result is None:
   325→        return
   326→    resolved_position, resolved_target, offset = result
   327→
   328→    count = move_items(plan, item_ids, resolved_position, target=resolved_target, offset=offset)
   329→    append_log_entry(
   330→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   331→        detail={"position": resolved_position, "count": count, "item": item_pattern},
   332→    )
   333→    save_plan(plan)
   334→    print(colorize(f"  Moved {count} item(s) to {resolved_position} within cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   335→
   336→
   337→def _reorder_whole_clusters(
   338→    plan: dict,
   339→    clusters: dict,
   340→    cluster_names: list[str],
   341→    position: str,
   342→    target: str | None,
   343→) -> None:
   344→    """Reorder entire clusters as blocks relative to each other."""
   345→    target = resolve_target(plan, target, position)
   346→
   347→    offset = None
   348→    if position in ("up", "down") and target is not None:
   349→        try:
   350→            offset = int(target)
   351→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   352→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   353→            return
   354→        target = None
   355→
   356→    seen: set[str] = set()
   357→    all_member_ids: list[str] = []
   358→    for name in cluster_names:
   359→        for fid in clusters[name].get("issue_ids", []):
   360→            if fid not in seen:
   361→                seen.add(fid)
   362→                all_member_ids.append(fid)
   363→
   364→    if not all_member_ids:
   365→        print(colorize("  No members in the specified cluster(s).", "yellow"))
   366→        return
   367→
   368→    count = move_items(plan, all_member_ids, position, target=target, offset=offset)
   369→    append_log_entry(
   370→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=",".join(cluster_names), actor="user",
   371→        detail={"position": position, "count": count},
   372→    )
   373→    save_plan(plan)
   374→    label = ", ".join(cluster_names)
   375→    print(colorize(f"  Moved cluster(s) {label} ({count} items) to {position}.", "green"))

   477→            _print_step(i, step)
   478→
   479→    # Members
   480→    issue_ids = cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   481→    print()
   482→    if not issue_ids:
   483→        print(colorize("  Members: (none)", "dim"))
   484→    else:
   485→        issues = _load_issues_best_effort(args)
   486→        print(colorize(f"  Members ({len(issue_ids)}):", "dim"))
   487→        for idx, fid in enumerate(issue_ids, 1):
   488→            _print_cluster_member(idx, fid, issues.get(fid))
   489→

   492→    print(colorize("  Commands:", "dim"))

   494→    print(colorize(f"    Drill in:     desloppify next --cluster {cluster_name} --count 10", "dim"))
   495→    print(colorize(f"    Skip:         desloppify plan skip {cluster_name}", "dim"))

   497→
   498→def _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(
   499→    clusters: dict, queue_order: list[str],
   500→) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, dict]], dict[str, int]]:
   501→    """Sort clusters by (priority, earliest queue position).
   502→
   503→    Clusters with explicit priority sort first (ascending), then unset-priority
   504→    clusters sort by queue position.
   505→
   506→    Returns (sorted_cluster_pairs, min_pos_cache) where min_pos_cache maps
   507→    cluster name to its earliest queue position (999_999 if no members queued).
   508→    """
   509→    pos_map = {fid: i for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order)}
   510→
   511→    def _min_pos(cluster_data: dict) -> int:
   512→        positions = [pos_map[fid] for fid in cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []) if fid in pos_map]
   513→        return min(positions) if positions else 999_999
   514→
   515→    min_pos_cache = {name: _min_pos(c) for name, c in clusters.items()}
   516→    sorted_clusters = sorted(
   517→        clusters.items(),
   518→        key=lambda kv: (kv[1].get("priority", 999), min_pos_cache[kv[0]]),
   519→    )
   520→    return sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache
   521→
   522→
   523→def _print_cluster_list_verbose(
   524→    sorted_clusters: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   525→    min_pos_cache: dict[str, int],
   526→    active: str | None,
   527→) -> None:
   528→    """Print the verbose table view of the cluster list."""
   529→    name_width = max(20, min(35, max(len(n) for n, _ in sorted_clusters)))
   530→    total = len(sorted_clusters)
   531→    has_dep = any(c.get("dependency_order") is not None for _, c in sorted_clusters)
   532→    print(colorize(f"  Clusters ({total} total, sorted by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   533→    print()
   534→    dep_header = f"  {'Dep':>3}" if has_dep else ""
   535→    header = f"  {'#pos':<5}  {'Pri':>3}{dep_header}  {'Name':<{name_width}}  {'Items':>5}  {'Steps':>5}  {'Type':<6}  Description"
   536→    dep_sep = f"  {'─'*3}" if has_dep else ""
   537→    sep = f"  {'─'*4}  {'─'*3}{dep_sep}  {'─'*name_width}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*6}  {'─'*40}"
   538→    print(colorize(header, "dim"))
   539→    print(colorize(sep, "dim"))
   540→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   541→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   542→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   543→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   544→        pri_str = str(priority) if priority is not None else "—"
   545→        dep_order = cluster.get("dependency_order")
   546→        dep_str = f"  {dep_order:>3}" if has_dep and dep_order is not None else ("  {:>3}".format("—") if has_dep else "")
   547→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   548→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   549→        steps_str = str(len(steps)) if steps else "—"
   550→        type_str = "auto" if cluster.get("auto") else "manual"
   551→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   552→        if not desc and min_p == 999_999 and not member_count:
   553→            desc = "(no queue position — no members)"
   554→        desc_truncated = (desc[:39] + "…") if len(desc) > 40 else desc
   555→        name_display = (name[:name_width - 1] + "…") if len(name) > name_width else name
   556→        focused = " *" if name == active else ""
   557→        print(f"  {pos_str:>5}  {pri_str:>3}{dep_str}  {name_display:<{name_width}}  {member_count:>5}  {steps_str:>5}  {type_str:<6}  {desc_truncated}{focused}")
   558→    print()

   561→def _cmd_cluster_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   562→    plan = load_plan()
   563→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   564→    active = plan.get("active_cluster")
   565→    verbose: bool = getattr(args, "verbose", False)
   566→    missing_steps: bool = getattr(args, "missing_steps", False)
   567→
   568→    if not clusters:
   569→        print("  No clusters defined.")
   570→        return
   571→
   572→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   573→    sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache = _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(clusters, queue_order)
   574→
   575→    if missing_steps:
   576→        from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage.stage_helpers import _unenriched_clusters
   577→        gaps = _unenriched_clusters(plan)
   578→        if not gaps:
   579→            print(colorize("  All clusters have action steps.", "green"))
   580→            return
   581→        print(colorize(f"  {len(gaps)} cluster(s) need action steps:", "bold"))
   582→        for name, missing in gaps:
   583→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}", "yellow"))
   584→        print()
   585→        print(colorize("  Fix with:", "dim"))
   586→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --description "..." --steps "step1" "step2"', "dim"))
   587→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --add-step "step title" --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   588→        return
   589→
   590→    if verbose:
   591→        _print_cluster_list_verbose(sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache, active)
   592→        return
   593→
   594→    print(colorize("  Clusters (ordered by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   595→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   596→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   597→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   598→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   599→        pri_tag = f" [P{priority}]" if priority is not None else ""
   600→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   601→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   602→        marker = " (focused)" if name == active else ""
   603→        desc_str = f" — {desc}" if desc else ""
   604→        auto_tag = " [auto]" if cluster.get("auto") else ""
   605→        print(f"    {pos_str:>5} {pri_tag} {name}: {member_count} items{auto_tag}{desc_str}{marker}")

   608→def _cmd_cluster_update(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   609→    """Update cluster description, steps, and/or priority."""
   610→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   611→    description: str | None = getattr(args, "description", None)
   612→    steps: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "steps", None)
   613→    steps_file: str | None = getattr(args, "steps_file", None)
   614→    add_step: str | None = getattr(args, "add_step", None)
   615→    detail: str | None = getattr(args, "detail", None)
   616→    update_step: int | None = getattr(args, "update_step", None)
   617→    remove_step: int | None = getattr(args, "remove_step", None)
   618→    done_step: int | None = getattr(args, "done_step", None)
   619→    undone_step: int | None = getattr(args, "undone_step", None)
   620→    priority: int | None = getattr(args, "priority", None)
   621→    effort: str | None = getattr(args, "effort", None)
   622→    depends_on: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "depends_on", None)
   623→    issue_refs: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "issue_refs", None)
   624→
   625→    has_update = any(x is not None for x in [
   626→        description, steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step,
   627→        remove_step, done_step, undone_step, priority, effort,
   628→        depends_on, issue_refs,
   629→    ])
   630→    if not has_update:
   631→        print(colorize("  Nothing to update. Use --description, --steps, --steps-file, --add-step, --priority, etc.", "yellow"))
   632→        return
   633→
   634→    plan = load_plan()
   635→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   636→    if cluster is None:
   637→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   638→        return
   639→
   640→    if description is not None:
   641→        cluster["description"] = description
   642→
   643→    if priority is not None:
   644→        cluster["priority"] = priority
   645→        print(colorize(f"  Priority set to {priority}.", "dim"))
   646→
   647→    if depends_on is not None:
   648→        all_clusters = set(plan.get("clusters", {}).keys())
   649→        bad = [n for n in depends_on if n not in all_clusters]
   650→        if bad:
   651→            print(colorize(f"  Unknown cluster(s): {', '.join(bad)}", "red"))
   652→            return
   653→        cluster["depends_on_clusters"] = depends_on
   654→        print(colorize(f"  Dependencies set: {', '.join(depends_on)}", "dim"))
   655→
   656→    # Steps replacement: --steps-file takes precedence over --steps
   657→    if steps_file is not None:
   658→        path = Path(steps_file)
   659→        if not path.is_file():
   660→            print(colorize(f"  Steps file not found: {steps_file}", "red"))
   661→            return
   662→        parsed = parse_steps_file(path.read_text())
   663→        cluster["action_steps"] = parsed
   664→        print(colorize(f"  Loaded {len(parsed)} step(s) from {steps_file}.", "dim"))
   665→    elif steps is not None:
   666→        # Legacy flat strings → wrap as ActionStep dicts
   667→        cluster["action_steps"] = [normalize_step(s) for s in steps]
   668→        print(colorize(f"  Stored {len(steps)} action step(s).", "dim"))
   669→
   670→    # Incremental step operations
   671→    current_steps: list = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   672→
   673→    MAX_STEP_TITLE = 150
   674→
   675→    if add_step is not None:
   676→        new_step: dict = {"title": add_step}
   677→        if detail is not None:
   678→            new_step["detail"] = detail
   679→        if effort is not None:
   680→            new_step["effort"] = effort
   681→        if issue_refs is not None:
   682→            new_step["issue_refs"] = issue_refs
   683→        if len(add_step) > MAX_STEP_TITLE:
   684→            print(colorize(
   685→                f"  Warning: step title is {len(add_step)} chars (recommended max {MAX_STEP_TITLE}).",
   686→                "yellow",
   687→            ))
   688→            print(colorize("  Move implementation detail to --detail instead.", "dim"))
   689→        current_steps.append(new_step)
   690→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   691→        print(colorize(f"  Added step {len(current_steps)}: {add_step}", "dim"))
   692→
   693→    if update_step is not None:
   694→        idx = update_step - 1
   695→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   696→            print(colorize(f"  Step {update_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   697→            return
   698→        old = current_steps[idx]
   699→        if isinstance(old, str):
   700→            old = {"title": old}
   701→        if add_step is None:
   702→            # When --update-step is used without --add-step, keep title, update detail only
   703→            if detail is not None:
   704→                old["detail"] = detail
   705→        else:
   706→            old["title"] = add_step
   707→            if detail is not None:
   708→                old["detail"] = detail
   709→            if len(add_step) > MAX_STEP_TITLE:
   710→                print(colorize(
   711→                    f"  Warning: step title is {len(add_step)} chars (recommended max {MAX_STEP_TITLE}).",
   712→                    "yellow",
   713→                ))
   714→                print(colorize("  Move implementation detail to --detail instead.", "dim"))
   715→        if effort is not None:
   716→            old["effort"] = effort
   717→        if issue_refs is not None:
   718→            old["issue_refs"] = issue_refs
   719→        current_steps[idx] = old
   720→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   721→        print(colorize(f"  Updated step {update_step}.", "dim"))
   722→
   723→    if remove_step is not None:
   724→        idx = remove_step - 1
   725→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   726→            print(colorize(f"  Step {remove_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   727→            return
   728→        removed = current_steps.pop(idx)
   729→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   730→        title = step_summary(removed)
   731→        print(colorize(f"  Removed step {remove_step}: {title}", "dim"))
   732→
   733→    if done_step is not None:
   734→        idx = done_step - 1
   735→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   736→            print(colorize(f"  Step {done_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   737→            return
   738→        step = current_steps[idx]
   739→        if isinstance(step, str):
   740→            step = {"title": step}
   741→            current_steps[idx] = step
   742→        step["done"] = True
   743→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   744→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {done_step} as done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   745→
   746→    if undone_step is not None:
   747→        idx = undone_step - 1
   748→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(current_steps):
   749→            print(colorize(f"  Step {undone_step} out of range (1-{len(current_steps)}).", "red"))
   750→            return
   751→        step = current_steps[idx]
   752→        if isinstance(step, str):
   753→            step = {"title": step}
   754→            current_steps[idx] = step
   755→        step["done"] = False
   756→        cluster["action_steps"] = current_steps
   757→        print(colorize(f"  Marked step {undone_step} as not done: {step.get('title', '')}", "dim"))
   758→
   759→    # Show resulting steps after any mutation
   760→    final_steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   761→    if final_steps and any(x is not None for x in [steps, steps_file, add_step, update_step, remove_step, done_step, undone_step]):
   762→        print()
   763→        print(colorize(f"  Current steps ({len(final_steps)}):", "dim"))
   764→        for i, s in enumerate(final_steps, 1):
   765→            _print_step(i, s)
   766→
   767→    cluster["user_modified"] = True
   768→    cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   769→    append_log_entry(
   770→        plan, "cluster_update", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   771→        detail={"description": description},
   772→    )
   773→    save_plan(plan)
   774→    print(colorize(f"  Updated cluster: {cluster_name}", "green"))
   775→

   777→def _cmd_cluster_export(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   778→    """Export cluster steps to stdout in text or YAML format."""
   779→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   780→    export_format: str = getattr(args, "export_format", "text")
   781→
   782→    plan = load_plan()
   783→    cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(cluster_name)
   784→    if cluster is None:
   785→        print(colorize(f"  Cluster {cluster_name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   786→        return
   787→
   788→    steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   789→    if not steps:
   790→        print(colorize("  No steps to export.", "yellow"))
   791→        return
   792→
   793→    if export_format == "yaml":
   794→        import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   795→        data = {
   796→            "clusters": [{
   797→                "name": cluster_name,
   798→                "description": cluster.get("description") or "",
   799→                **({"priority": cluster["priority"]} if "priority" in cluster else {}),
   800→                "steps": [
   801→                    normalize_step(s) for s in steps
   802→                ],
   803→            }]
   804→        }
   805→        print(yaml.dump(data, default_flow_style=False, sort_keys=False))
   806→    else:
   807→        print(format_steps(steps))
   808→
   809→
   810→def _cmd_cluster_import(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   811→    """Bulk create/update clusters from a YAML file."""
   812→    file_path: str = getattr(args, "file", "")
   813→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   814→
   815→    path = Path(file_path)
   816→    if not path.is_file():
   817→        print(colorize(f"  File not found: {file_path}", "red"))
   818→        return
   819→
   820→    import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   821→    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
   822→    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "clusters" not in data:
   823→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: expected top-level 'clusters' key.", "red"))
   824→        return
   825→
   826→    entries = data["clusters"]
   827→    if not isinstance(entries, list):
   828→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: 'clusters' must be a list.", "red"))
   829→        return
   830→
   831→    plan = load_plan()
   832→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   833→    created = 0
   834→    updated = 0
   835→
   836→    for entry in entries:
   837→        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "name" not in entry:
   838→            print(colorize(f"  Skipping entry without 'name': {entry!r}", "yellow"))
   839→            continue
   840→        name = entry["name"]
   841→        is_new = name not in clusters
   842→
   843→        if dry_run:
   844→            action = "CREATE" if is_new else "UPDATE"
   845→            step_count = len(entry.get("steps", []))
   846→            print(colorize(f"  [{action}] {name}: {step_count} step(s)", "cyan"))
   847→            continue
   848→
   849→        if is_new:
   850→            try:
   851→                cluster = create_cluster(plan, name, entry.get("description"))
   852→            except ValueError as ex:
   853→                print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   854→                continue
   855→            created += 1
   856→        else:
   857→            cluster = clusters[name]
   858→            updated += 1
   859→
   860→        if "description" in entry:
   861→            cluster["description"] = entry["description"]
   862→        if "priority" in entry:
   863→            cluster["priority"] = entry["priority"]
   864→        if "steps" in entry:
   865→            imported_steps = []
   866→            for s in entry["steps"]:
   867→                if isinstance(s, str):
   868→                    imported_steps.append({"title": s})
   869→                elif isinstance(s, dict):
   870→                    step: dict = {"title": s.get("title", "")}
   871→                    if "detail" in s:
   872→                        step["detail"] = s["detail"]
   873→                    if "refs" in s:
   874→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["refs"]
   875→                    elif "issue_refs" in s:
   876→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["issue_refs"]
   877→                    imported_steps.append(step)
   878→            cluster["action_steps"] = imported_steps
   879→        cluster["user_modified"] = True
   880→        cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   881→
   882→    if dry_run:
   883→        print(colorize("  (dry run — no changes saved)", "dim"))
   884→        return
   885→
   886→    save_plan(plan)
   887→    print(colorize(f"  Import complete: {created} created, {updated} updated.", "green"))
   888→
   889→
   890→def _cmd_cluster_merge(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   891→    """Merge source cluster into target cluster."""
   892→    source: str = getattr(args, "source", "")
   893→    target: str = getattr(args, "target", "")
   894→
   895→    plan = load_plan()
   896→    try:
   897→        added, source_ids = merge_clusters(plan, source, target)
   898→    except ValueError as ex:
   899→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   900→        return
   901→
   902→    append_log_entry(
   903→        plan, "cluster_merge", issue_ids=source_ids,
   904→        cluster_name=target, actor="user",
   905→        detail={"source": source, "added": added},
   906→    )
   907→    save_plan(plan)
   908→    print(colorize(
   909→        f"  Merged cluster {source!r} into {target!r}: "
   910→        f"{added} issue(s) added, {len(source_ids)} total moved. Source deleted.",
   911→        "green",
   912→    ))
   913→
   914→
   915→def cmd_cluster_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   916→    """Route cluster subcommands."""
   917→    cluster_action = getattr(args, "cluster_action", None)
   918→    dispatch = {
   919→        "create": _cmd_cluster_create,
   920→        "add": _cmd_cluster_add,
   921→        "remove": _cmd_cluster_remove,
   922→        "delete": _cmd_cluster_delete,
   923→        "reorder": _cmd_cluster_reorder,
   924→        "show": _cmd_cluster_show,
   925→        "list": _cmd_cluster_list,
   926→        "update": _cmd_cluster_update,
   927→        "merge": _cmd_cluster_merge,
   928→        "export": _cmd_cluster_export,
   929→        "import": _cmd_cluster_import,
   930→    }
   931→    handler = dispatch.get(cluster_action)
   932→    if handler is None:
   933→        _cmd_cluster_list(args)
   934→        return
   935→    handler(args)
   936→
   937→
   938→__all__ = ["cmd_cluster_dispatch"]
   939→

    62→    output = getattr(args, "output", None)

   100→def _cmd_plan_show(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:

   109→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:

   111→        ordered = len(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   112→        queue_line = f"Queue: {ordered} items prioritized"
   113→
   114→    skipped = plan.get("skipped", {})
   115→    total_skipped = len(skipped)
   116→    kind_counts = {
   117→        kind: sum(1 for entry in skipped.values() if entry.get("kind") == kind)
   118→        for kind in USER_SKIP_KINDS
   119→    }
   120→    temp_count = kind_counts["temporary"]
   121→    perm_count = kind_counts["permanent"]
   122→    fp_count = kind_counts["false_positive"]
   123→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})

   125→    superseded = len(plan.get("superseded", {}))
   126→
   127→    described, noted = annotation_counts(plan)
   128→
   129→    print(colorize("  Living Plan Status", "bold"))
   130→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 40, "dim"))
   131→    print(f"  {queue_line}")
   132→    if total_skipped:
   133→        print(f"  Skipped:          {total_skipped} (temp: {temp_count}, wontfix: {perm_count}, fp: {fp_count})")
   134→    else:
   135→        print("  Skipped:          0")
   136→    print(f"  Clusters:         {len(clusters)}")
   137→    if clusters:
   138→        for name, cluster in clusters.items():
   139→            desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   140→            member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   141→            marker = " (focused)" if name == active else ""
   142→            desc_str = f" — {desc}" if desc else ""
   143→            print(f"    {name}: {member_count} items{desc_str}{marker}")
   144→    if described or noted:
   145→        print(f"  Annotations:      {described} described, {noted} noted")
   146→    if active:
   147→        print(f"  Focus:            {active}")
   148→    if superseded:
   149→        print(f"  Disappeared:      {superseded} (resolved or removed since last scan)")
   150→
   151→    # Commit tracking summary
   152→    _cfg = load_config()
   153→    if _cfg.get("commit_tracking_enabled", True):
   154→        ct = commit_tracking_summary(plan)
   155→        if ct["total"] > 0:

   158→            print(
