   158→
   159→def _cmd_stage_reflect(
   160→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   161→    *,
   162→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   163→) -> None:
   164→    """Record the REFLECT stage: compare current issues against completed work.
   165→
   166→    Forces the agent to consider what was previously resolved and whether
   167→    similar issues are recurring. Requires a 100-char report (50 if ≤3 issues).
   168→    If recurring patterns are detected, the report must mention at least one
   169→    recurring dimension name.
   170→    """
   171→    report: str | None = getattr(args, "report", None)
   172→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   173→
   174→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   175→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   176→    state = runtime.state
   177→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   178→
   179→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   180→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to reflect on.", "yellow"))
   181→        return
   182→
   183→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   184→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   185→
   186→    # Jump-back: reuse existing report if no --report provided
   187→    existing_stage = stages.get("reflect")
   188→    is_reuse = False
   189→    if not report and existing_stage and existing_stage.get("report"):
   190→        report = existing_stage["report"]
   191→        is_reuse = True
   192→    elif not report:
   193→        _print_reflect_report_requirement()
   194→        return
   195→
   196→    if "observe" not in stages:
   197→        print(colorize("  Cannot reflect: observe stage not complete.", "red"))
   198→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage observe --report "..."', "dim"))
   199→        return
   200→
   201→    si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, state)
   202→
   203→    # Fold-confirm: auto-confirm observe if attestation provided
   204→    if not _auto_confirm_observe_if_attested(
   205→        plan=plan,
   206→        stages=stages,
   207→        attestation=attestation,
   208→        triage_input=si,
   209→    ):
   210→        return
   211→
   212→    issue_count = len(si.open_issues)
   213→
   214→    # Validation: report length
   215→    min_chars = 50 if issue_count <= 3 else 100
   216→    if len(report) < min_chars:
   217→        print(colorize(f"  Report too short: {len(report)} chars (minimum {min_chars}).", "red"))
   218→        print(colorize("  Describe how current issues relate to previously completed work.", "dim"))
   219→        return
   220→
   221→    # Detect recurring patterns
   222→    recurring = resolved_services.detect_recurring_patterns(
   223→        si.open_issues,
   224→        si.resolved_issues,
   225→    )
   226→    recurring_dims = sorted(recurring.keys())
   227→
   228→    # If recurring patterns exist, report must mention at least one dimension
   229→    if not _validate_recurring_dimension_mentions(
   230→        report=report,
   231→        recurring_dims=recurring_dims,
   232→        recurring=recurring,
   233→    ):
   234→        return
   235→
   236→    # Save stage
   237→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   238→    reflect_stage = {
   239→        "stage": "reflect",
   240→        "report": report,
   241→        "cited_ids": [],
   242→        "timestamp": utc_now(),
   243→        "issue_count": issue_count,
   244→    }
   245→    reflect_stage["recurring_dims"] = recurring_dims
   246→    stages["reflect"] = reflect_stage
   247→
   248→    # Jump-back: preserve or clear confirmation
   249→    if is_reuse and existing_stage and existing_stage.get("confirmed_at"):
   250→        stages["reflect"]["confirmed_at"] = existing_stage["confirmed_at"]
   251→        stages["reflect"]["confirmed_text"] = existing_stage.get("confirmed_text", "")
   252→    cleared = cascade_clear_later_confirmations(stages, "reflect")
   253→
   254→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   255→
   256→    reflect_detail = {
   257→        "issue_count": issue_count,
   258→        "reuse": is_reuse,
   259→    }
   260→    reflect_detail["recurring_dims"] = recurring_dims
   261→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   262→        plan,
   263→        "triage_reflect",
   264→        actor="user",
   265→        detail=reflect_detail,
   266→    )
   267→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   268→
   269→    print_reflect_result(
   270→        issue_count=issue_count,
   271→        recurring_dims=recurring_dims,
   272→        recurring=recurring,
   273→        report=report,
   274→        is_reuse=is_reuse,
   275→        cleared=cleared,
   276→        stages=stages,
   277→    )
   278→
   279→
   280→def _cmd_stage_organize(
   281→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   282→    *,
   283→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   284→) -> None:
   285→    """Record the ORGANIZE stage: validates cluster enrichment.
   286→
   287→    Instead of gating on a text report, validates that the plan data
   288→    itself has been enriched: each manual cluster needs description +
   289→    action_steps. This forces the agent to actually think about each
   290→    cluster's execution plan.
   291→    """
   292→    report: str | None = getattr(args, "report", None)
   293→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   294→
   295→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   296→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   297→
   298→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   299→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to organize.", "yellow"))
   300→        return
   301→
   302→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   303→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   304→
   305→    # Jump-back: reuse existing report if no --report provided
   306→    existing_stage = stages.get("organize")
   307→    is_reuse = False
   308→    if not report and existing_stage and existing_stage.get("report"):
   309→        report = existing_stage["report"]
   310→        is_reuse = True
   311→
   312→    if not _require_reflect_stage_for_organize(stages):
   313→        return
   314→
   315→    # Fold-confirm: auto-confirm reflect if attestation provided
   316→    if not _auto_confirm_reflect_for_organize(
   317→        args=args,
   318→        plan=plan,
   319→        stages=stages,
   320→        attestation=attestation,
   321→    ):
   322→        return
   323→
   324→    # Validate: at least 1 manual cluster with issues
   325→    manual_clusters = _manual_clusters_or_error(plan)
   326→    if manual_clusters is None:
   327→        return
   328→
   329→    # Validate: all manual clusters are enriched
   330→    if not _clusters_enriched_or_error(plan):
   331→        return
   332→
   333→    # Validate: all review issues are in a manual cluster (or wontfixed)
   334→    state = resolved_services.command_runtime(args).state
   335→    if not _unclustered_review_issues_or_error(plan, state):
   336→        return
   337→
   338→    # Warn if few/no cluster operations since reflect
   339→    reflect_ts = stages.get("reflect", {}).get("timestamp", "")
   340→    if reflect_ts and not is_reuse:
   341→        activity = count_log_activity_since(plan, reflect_ts)
   342→        cluster_ops = sum(
   343→            activity.get(k, 0)
   344→            for k in ("cluster_create", "cluster_add", "cluster_update", "cluster_remove")
   345→        )
   346→        if cluster_ops == 0:
   347→            print(colorize("  Warning: no cluster operations logged since reflect.", "yellow"))
   348→            print(colorize("  Did you create clusters, add issues, and enrich them?", "yellow"))
   349→            print(colorize("  The organize stage should reflect real work — not just recording a report.", "dim"))
   350→            print()
   351→        elif cluster_ops < 3:
   352→            print(colorize(f"  Note: only {cluster_ops} cluster operation(s) logged since reflect.", "yellow"))
   353→            print(colorize("  Make sure all clusters are properly set up before proceeding.", "dim"))
   354→            print()
   355→
   356→    report = _organize_report_or_error(report)
   357→    if report is None:
   358→        return
   359→
   360→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   361→    cleared = _record_organize_stage(
   362→        stages,
   363→        report=report,
   364→        issue_count=len(manual_clusters),
   365→        existing_stage=existing_stage,
   366→        is_reuse=is_reuse,
   367→    )
   368→
   369→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   370→
   371→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   372→        plan,
   373→        "triage_organize",
   374→        actor="user",
   375→        detail={"cluster_count": len(manual_clusters), "reuse": is_reuse},
   376→    )
   377→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   378→
   379→    print_organize_result(
   380→        manual_clusters=manual_clusters,
   381→        plan=plan,
   382→        report=report,
   383→        is_reuse=is_reuse,
   384→        cleared=cleared,
   385→        stages=stages,
   386→    )

   388→
   389→def _cmd_stage_enrich(
   390→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   391→    *,
   392→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   393→) -> None:
   394→    """Record the ENRICH stage: validate steps have detail/refs for executor readiness.
   395→
   396→    This stage sits between organize and commit. It checks whether action steps
   397→    are detailed enough for an executor with zero context. Steps should have
   398→    ``detail`` (sub-points) and/or ``issue_refs`` (for auto-completion).
   399→
   400→    The agent can still go back and organize (add/remove clusters, reorder)
   401→    at this point — the stage just validates step quality.
   402→    """
   403→    report: str | None = getattr(args, "report", None)
   404→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   405→
   406→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   407→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   408→
   409→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   410→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to enrich.", "yellow"))
   411→        return
   412→
   413→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   414→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   415→
   416→    # Jump-back: reuse existing report if no --report provided
   417→    existing_stage = stages.get("enrich")
   418→    report, is_reuse = _resolve_reusable_report(report, existing_stage)
   419→
   420→    if not _require_organize_stage_for_enrich(stages):
   421→        return
   422→
   423→    # Auto-confirm organize if attestation provided
   424→    if not stages.get("organize", {}).get("confirmed_at"):
   425→        if attestation:
   426→            from ._stage_validation import _auto_confirm_organize_for_complete
   427→            if not _auto_confirm_organize_for_complete(
   428→                plan=plan, stages=stages, attestation=attestation,
   429→            ):
   430→                return
   431→        else:
   432→            print(colorize("  Cannot enrich: organize stage not confirmed.", "red"))
   433→            print(colorize("  Run: desloppify plan triage --confirm organize", "dim"))
   434→            print(colorize("  Or pass --attestation to auto-confirm organize inline.", "dim"))
   435→            return
   436→
   437→    # Check shallow steps — block if any steps lack detail or issue_refs
   438→    shallow = _shallow_steps(plan)
   439→    total_bare = sum(n for _, n, _ in shallow)
   440→
   441→    if shallow:
   442→        print(colorize(f"  Cannot enrich: {total_bare} step(s) across {len(shallow)} cluster(s) lack detail or issue_refs:", "red"))
   443→        for name, bare, total in shallow:
   444→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {bare}/{total} steps need enrichment", "yellow"))
   445→        print()
   446→        print(colorize("  Every step needs --detail (sub-points) or --issue-refs (for auto-completion).", "dim"))
   447→        print(colorize("  Fix:", "dim"))
   448→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   449→        print(colorize("  You can also still reorganize: add/remove clusters, reorder, etc.", "dim"))
   450→        return
   451→    else:
   452→        print(colorize("  All steps have detail or issue_refs.", "green"))
   453→
   454→    # Advisory: check for bad file paths in step details
   455→    from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
   456→    bad_paths = _steps_with_bad_paths(plan, get_project_root())
   457→    if bad_paths:
   458→        total_bad = sum(len(bp) for _, _, bp in bad_paths)
   459→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {total_bad} file path(s) in step details don't exist on disk:", "yellow"))
   460→        for name, step_num, paths in bad_paths[:5]:
   461→            print(colorize(f"    {name} step {step_num}: {', '.join(paths[:3])}", "yellow"))
   462→        print(colorize("  Fix paths before confirming enrich (confirmation will block on bad paths).", "dim"))
   463→
   464→    # Advisory: check for missing effort tags
   465→    untagged = _steps_without_effort(plan)
   466→    if untagged:
   467→        total_missing = sum(n for _, n, _ in untagged)
   468→        print(colorize(f"  Note: {total_missing} step(s) have no effort tag.", "yellow"))
   469→        print(colorize("  Consider: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --effort small", "dim"))
   470→
   471→    report = _enrich_report_or_error(report)
   472→    if report is None:
   473→        return
   474→
   475→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   476→    cleared = _record_enrich_stage(
   477→        stages,
   478→        report=report,
   479→        shallow_count=total_bare,
   480→        existing_stage=existing_stage,
   481→        is_reuse=is_reuse,
   482→    )
   483→
   484→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   485→
   486→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   487→        plan,
   488→        "triage_enrich",
   489→        actor="user",
   490→        detail={"shallow_count": total_bare, "reuse": is_reuse},
   491→    )
   492→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   493→
   494→    print(colorize(
   495→        f"  Enrich stage recorded: {total_bare} step(s) still without detail.",
   496→        "green",
   497→    ))
   498→    if is_reuse:
   499→        print(colorize("  Enrich data preserved (no changes).", "dim"))
   500→        if cleared:
   501→            print_cascade_clear_feedback(cleared, stages)
   502→    else:
   503→        print(colorize("  Now confirm the enrichment.", "yellow"))
   504→        print(colorize("    desloppify plan triage --confirm enrich", "dim"))
   505→
   506→    print_user_message(
   507→        "Hey — enrich is recorded. Before confirming, double-check"
   508→        " that every step is clear enough for an executor with zero"
   509→        " context. Add --detail to any step that's too vague. You"
   510→        " can still reorganize at this point (add/remove clusters,"
   511→        " reorder items). Once satisfied, confirm and complete triage."
   512→    )
   513→
   514→
   515→def cmd_stage_observe(
   516→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   517→    *,
   518→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   519→) -> None:
   520→    """Public entrypoint for observe stage recording."""
   521→    _cmd_stage_observe(args, services=services)
   522→

   525→    args: argparse.Namespace,

   532→
   533→def cmd_stage_enrich(

1→"""Runtime compatibility governance matrix and helper predicates.
     2→
     3→This module is the single source of truth for import-boundary policy:
     4→- public runtime modules (stable entry surfaces),
     5→- deprecated compatibility modules (removal candidates),
     6→- private modules (internal implementation details).
     7→"""
     8→
     9→from __future__ import annotations
    10→
    11→from collections.abc import Iterable
    12→
    13→# Public package roots intended for runtime imports across the codebase.
    14→PUBLIC_RUNTIME_ROOTS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    15→    "desloppify.app",
    16→    "desloppify.base",
    17→    "desloppify.engine",
    18→    "desloppify.intelligence",
    19→    "desloppify.languages",
    20→)
    21→
    22→# Compatibility shims removed from runtime usage; these must not be reintroduced.
    23→SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    24→    {
    25→        "desloppify.utils",
    26→        "desloppify.file_discovery",
    27→        "desloppify.base.output_api",
    28→        "desloppify.base.output_contract",
    29→        "desloppify.base.text.text_api",
    30→        "desloppify.base.discovery.api",
    31→        "desloppify.base.discovery.path_io",
    32→    }
    33→)
    34→
    35→SOFT_DEPRECATED_SHORT_IMPORTS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    36→    {
    37→        "utils",
    38→        "file_discovery",
    39→    }
    40→)
    41→
    42→# Private internals: only code under these roots may import them directly.
    43→PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    44→PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ("desloppify.base",)
    45→
    46→
    47→def is_soft_deprecated_module(module: str) -> bool:
    48→    """Return True when module is a soft-deprecated compatibility surface."""
    49→    return module in SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES
    50→
    51→
    52→def is_private_module(module: str) -> bool:
    53→    """Return True when module path belongs to a private internal namespace."""
    54→    normalized = module.strip()
    55→    if not normalized:
    56→        return False
    57→    for prefix in PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES:
    58→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    59→            return True
    60→    return False
    61→
    62→
    63→def importer_can_access_private(importer_module: str) -> bool:
    64→    """Return True when importer module is allowed to reference private APIs."""
    65→    normalized = importer_module.strip()
    66→    if not normalized:
    67→        return False
    68→    for prefix in PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES:
    69→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    70→            return True
    71→    return False
    72→
    73→
    74→def iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths() -> Iterable[str]:
    75→    """Yield python-module relative paths for deprecated compatibility modules."""
    76→    for module in sorted(SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES):
    77→        parts = module.split(".")
    78→        yield "/".join(parts) + ".py"
    79→
    80→
    81→__all__ = [
    82→    "PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES",
    83→    "PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES",
    84→    "PUBLIC_RUNTIME_ROOTS",
    85→    "SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES",
    86→    "SOFT_DEPRECATED_SHORT_IMPORTS",
    87→    "importer_can_access_private",
    88→    "is_private_module",
    89→    "is_soft_deprecated_module",
    90→    "iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths",
    91→]
    92→

   153→def _cmd_confirm_existing(
   154→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   155→    *,
   156→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   157→) -> None:
   158→    """Fast-track: confirm existing plan structure is still valid."""
   159→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   160→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   161→    strategy: str | None = getattr(args, "strategy", None)

   163→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()

   165→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):

   169→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   170→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})

   172→    # Require a prior completed triage — can't skip the full flow on first run
   173→    if not _require_prior_strategy_for_confirm(meta):
   174→        return
   175→
   176→    # Determine if this is a light-path (additions only) or full ceremony
   177→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   178→    state = runtime.state
   179→    si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, state)
   180→    has_only_additions = bool(si.new_since_last) and not si.resolved_since_last
   181→
   182→    if not _confirm_existing_stages_valid(

   194→        return

   196→    # Require note

   199→
   200→    # Require strategy (default to "same" on light path)

   209→    # Strategy length check (unless "same")
   210→    if not _confirm_strategy_valid(strategy):
   211→        return
   212→
   213→    # Require --confirmed with plan review
   214→    confirmed_text = _confirmed_text_or_error(
   215→        plan=plan,
   216→        state=state,
   217→        confirmed=confirmed,
   218→    )
   219→    if confirmed_text is None:
   220→        return
   221→
   222→    # Validate: note cites at least 1 new/changed issue (if there are any)
   223→    if not _note_cites_new_issues_or_error(note, si):
   224→        return
   225→
   226→    # Record organize as confirmed-existing and complete
   227→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   228→    _record_confirm_existing_completion(
   229→        stages=stages,
   230→        note=note,
   231→        issue_count=len(clusters_with_issues),
   232→        confirmed_text=confirmed_text,
   233→    )
   234→
   235→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   236→        plan,
   237→        "triage_confirm_existing",
   238→        actor="user",
   239→        detail={"confirmed_text": confirmed_text},
   240→    )
   241→
   242→    apply_completion(args, plan, strategy, services=resolved_services)
   243→    print(colorize("  Confirmed existing plan — triage complete.", "green"))
   244→

     4→
     5→import argparse
     6→import logging
     7→
     8→from desloppify import state as state_mod
     9→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.query import (
    10→    write_query_best_effort as _write_query_best_effort,
    11→)
    12→from desloppify.base.exception_sets import PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS
    13→from desloppify.engine.plan import has_living_plan, load_plan
    14→
    15→from .selection import ResolveQueryContext
    16→
    17→_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18→
    19→
    20→def _try_expand_cluster(pattern: str) -> list[str] | None:
    21→    """If pattern matches a cluster name, return its issue IDs."""
    22→    try:
    23→        if not has_living_plan():
    24→            return None
    25→        plan = load_plan()
    26→        cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(pattern)
    27→        if cluster and cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    28→            return list(cluster["issue_ids"])
    29→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    30→        _logger.debug("cluster expansion skipped for %r", pattern, exc_info=True)
    31→    return None
    32→
    33→
    34→def _resolve_all_patterns(
    35→    state: dict,
    36→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    37→    *,
    38→    attestation: str | None,
    39→) -> list[str]:
    40→    all_resolved: list[str] = []
    41→    for pattern in args.patterns:
    42→        # Check if pattern is a cluster name — expand to member IDs
    43→        cluster_ids = _try_expand_cluster(pattern)
    44→        if cluster_ids:
    45→            for fid in cluster_ids:
    46→                resolved = state_mod.resolve_issues(
    47→                    state,
    48→                    fid,
    49→                    args.status,
    50→                    args.note,
    51→                    attestation=attestation,
    52→                )
    53→                all_resolved.extend(resolved)
    54→            continue
    55→
    56→        resolved = state_mod.resolve_issues(
    57→            state,
    58→            pattern,
    59→            args.status,
    60→            args.note,
    61→            attestation=attestation,
    62→        )
    63→        all_resolved.extend(resolved)
    64→    return all_resolved
    65→
    66→def _write_resolve_query_entry(context: ResolveQueryContext) -> None:
    67→    scores = state_mod.score_snapshot(context.state)
    68→    _write_query_best_effort(
    69→        {
    70→            "command": "resolve",
    71→            "patterns": context.patterns,
    72→            "status": context.status,
    73→            "resolved": context.resolved,
    74→            "count": len(context.resolved),
    75→            "next_command": context.next_command,
    76→            "overall_score": scores.overall,
    77→            "objective_score": scores.objective,
    78→            "strict_score": scores.strict,
    79→            "verified_strict_score": scores.verified,
    80→            "prev_overall_score": context.prev_overall,
    81→            "prev_objective_score": context.prev_objective,

    83→            "prev_verified_strict_score": context.prev_verified,
    84→            "attestation": context.attestation,
    85→            "narrative": context.narrative,
    86→        },
    87→        context="resolve query payload update",
    88→    )

1→"""Shared regex policies for migration/auth signal detection."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import re
     6→
     7→DEPRECATION_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"@[Dd]eprecated\b|DEPRECATED", re.MULTILINE)
     8→
     9→MIGRATION_TODO_RE = re.compile(
    10→    r"(?:TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b(?:\s*:)?[^\n]*\b(?:migrat\w*|legacy|deprecat\w*|old.?api|remove.?after)\b",
    11→    re.IGNORECASE,
    12→)
    13→
    14→SERVICE_ROLE_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(
    15→    r"\b(?:service[_-]?role(?:_key)?|serviceRole(?:Key)?|SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE(?:_KEY)?)\b",
    16→    re.IGNORECASE,
    17→)
    18→
    19→SERVER_ONLY_PATH_HINTS = (
    20→    "/api/",
    21→    "/server/",
    22→    "/backend/",
    23→    "/functions/",
    24→    "/supabase/functions/",
    25→    "/scripts/",
    26→)
    27→
    28→
    29→def is_server_only_path(path: str) -> bool:
    30→    """Best-effort classification for server-only source paths."""
    31→    if not path:
    32→        return False
    33→    normalized = path.replace("\\", "/")
    34→    prefixed = normalized if normalized.startswith("/") else f"/{normalized}"
    35→    return any(hint in prefixed for hint in SERVER_ONLY_PATH_HINTS)
    36→

    37→def print_stage_progress(stages: dict, plan: dict | None = None) -> None:

    40→    for stage_name, label in TRIAGE_STAGE_LABELS:
    41→        if stage_name in stages:
    42→            if stages[stage_name].get("confirmed_at"):
    43→                print(colorize(f"    \u2713 {label} (confirmed)", "green"))
    44→            else:
    45→                print(colorize(f"    \u2713 {label} (needs confirm)", "yellow"))
    46→        elif TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES[stage_name].issubset(stages):
    47→            print(colorize(f"    \u2192 {label} (current)", "yellow"))
    48→        else:
    49→            print(colorize(f"    \u25cb {label}", "dim"))
    50→
    51→    # Show enrichment gaps when in the organize stage

    53→        gaps = _unenriched_clusters(plan)
    54→        manual = manual_clusters_with_issues(plan)
    55→        if not manual:
    56→            print(colorize("\n    No manual clusters yet. Create clusters and enrich them.", "yellow"))

   383→def _print_issues_by_dimension(open_issues: dict) -> None:
   384→    """Print issues grouped by dimension with suggestions to surface contradictions."""
   385→    by_dim: dict[str, list[tuple[str, dict]]] = defaultdict(list)
   386→    for fid, f in open_issues.items():
   387→        detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
   388→        dim = detail.get("dimension", "unknown")
   389→        by_dim[dim].append((fid, f))
   390→
   391→    print(colorize("\n  Review issues by dimension:", "cyan"))
   392→    print(colorize("  (Look for contradictions: issues in the same dimension that", "dim"))
   393→    print(colorize("  recommend opposite changes. These must be resolved before clustering.)", "dim"))
   394→    max_per_dim = 5
   395→    for dim in sorted(by_dim, key=lambda d: (-len(by_dim[d]), d)):
   396→        items = by_dim[dim]
   397→        print(colorize(f"\n    {dim} ({len(items)}):", "bold"))
   398→        for fid, f in items[:max_per_dim]:
   399→            summary = f.get("summary", "")
   400→            short = short_issue_id(fid)
   401→            detail = f.get("detail", {}) if isinstance(f.get("detail"), dict) else {}
   402→            suggestion = (detail.get("suggestion") or "")[:120]
   403→            print(f"      [{short}] {summary}")
   404→            if suggestion:
   405→                print(colorize(f"        \u2192 {suggestion}", "dim"))
   406→        if len(items) > max_per_dim:
   407→            print(colorize(f"      ... and {len(items) - max_per_dim} more", "dim"))
   408→    print(colorize("\n  Use hash in commands: desloppify plan skip <hash>  |  desloppify show <hash>", "dim"))

   411→def cmd_triage_dashboard(
   412→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   413→    *,
   414→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   415→) -> None:
   416→    """Default view: show issues, stage progress, and next command."""
   417→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   418→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   419→    state = runtime.state
   420→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   421→    si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, state)
   422→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   423→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   424→
   425→    _print_dashboard_header(si, stages, meta, plan)
   426→    _print_action_guidance(stages, meta, si, plan)

   429→
   430→    # Show reflect dashboard when observe done, reflect not done

   432→        print_reflect_dashboard(si, plan, services=resolved_services)

   434→    # Show current cluster progress
   435→    print_progress(plan, si.open_issues)

   437→def show_plan_summary(plan: dict, state: dict) -> None:
   438→    """Print a compact plan rendering: clusters + queue order + coverage."""
   439→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   440→    active = {
   441→        n: c for n, c in clusters.items()
   442→        if c.get("issue_ids") and not c.get("auto")
   443→    }
   444→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   445→
   446→    if active:
   447→        print(colorize(f"\n  Clusters ({len(active)}):", "bold"))
   448→        for name, cluster in active.items():
   449→            count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   450→            steps = len(cluster.get("action_steps", []))
   451→            desc = (cluster.get("description") or "")[:60]
   452→            print(f"    {name}: {count} items, {steps} steps — {desc}")
   453→
   454→    queue_order = [
   455→        fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   456→        if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::")
   457→    ]
   458→    if queue_order:
   459→        show = min(15, len(queue_order))
   460→        print(colorize(f"\n  Queue order (first {show} of {len(queue_order)}):", "bold"))
   461→        for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order[:show]):
   462→            f = issues.get(fid, {})
   463→            summary = (f.get("summary") or fid)[:60]
   464→            detector = f.get("detector", "?")
   465→            cn = find_cluster_for(fid, active)
   466→            print(f"    {i+1}. [{detector}] {summary}{f' ({cn})' if cn else ''}")
   467→
   468→    organized, total, _ = triage_coverage(
   469→        plan, open_review_ids=open_review_ids_from_state(state),
   470→    )
   471→    pct = int(organized / total * 100) if total else 0
   472→    print(colorize(f"\n  Coverage: {organized}/{total} in clusters ({pct}%)", "bold"))
   473→

    53→        raise CommandError("Manual resolve requires a valid attestation.")
    54→
    55→
    56→def _previous_score_snapshot(state: dict) -> state_mod.ScoreSnapshot:
    57→    """Load a score snapshot for comparison after resolve operations."""
    58→    return state_mod.score_snapshot(state)
    59→
    60→
    61→def _preview_resolve_count(state: dict, patterns: list[str]) -> int:
    62→    """Count unique open issues matching the provided patterns."""
    63→    matched_ids: set[str] = set()
    64→    for pattern in patterns:
    65→        for issue in state_mod.match_issues(state, pattern, status_filter="open"):
    66→            issue_id = issue.get("id")
    67→            if issue_id:
    68→                matched_ids.add(issue_id)
    69→    return len(matched_ids)
    70→
    71→
    72→def _estimate_wontfix_strict_delta(
    73→    state: dict,
    74→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    75→    *,
    76→    attestation: str | None,
    77→    resolve_all_patterns_fn,
    78→) -> float:
    79→    """Estimate strict score drop if this resolve command is applied as wontfix."""
    80→    before = state_mod.score_snapshot(state).strict
    81→    if before is None:
    82→        return 0.0
    83→
    84→    preview_state = copy.deepcopy(state)
    85→    resolve_all_patterns_fn(preview_state, args, attestation=attestation)
    86→    after = state_mod.score_snapshot(preview_state).strict
    87→    if after is None:
    88→        return 0.0
    89→    return max(0.0, before - after)
    90→
    91→
    92→def _enforce_batch_wontfix_confirmation(
    93→    state: dict,
    94→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    95→    *,
    96→    attestation: str | None,
    97→    resolve_all_patterns_fn,
    98→) -> None:
    99→    if args.status != "wontfix":
   100→        return
   101→
   102→    preview_count = _preview_resolve_count(state, args.patterns)
   103→    if preview_count <= 10:
   104→        return
   105→    if getattr(args, "confirm_batch_wontfix", False):
   106→        return
   107→
   108→    strict_delta = _estimate_wontfix_strict_delta(
   109→        state,
   110→        args,
   111→        attestation=attestation,
   112→        resolve_all_patterns_fn=resolve_all_patterns_fn,
   113→    )
   114→    _emit_warning(f"Large wontfix batch detected ({preview_count} issues).")
   115→    if strict_delta > 0:
   116→        _emit_warning(f"Estimated strict-score debt added now: {strict_delta:.1f} points.")
   117→    raise CommandError(
   118→        "Re-run with --confirm-batch-wontfix if this debt is intentional."
   119→    )

1→"""Payload parsing helpers for review import workflows."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from dataclasses import dataclass
     6→from typing import Any
     7→
     8→from desloppify.intelligence.review.importing.contracts_types import (
     9→    ReviewImportPayload,
    10→    ReviewIssuePayload,
    11→)
    12→
    13→LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS_SUNSET_DATE = "2026-12-31"
    14→ALLOW_LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS = True
    15→
    16→
    17→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    18→class ReviewImportEnvelope:
    19→    """Validated shared payload shape for review imports."""
    20→
    21→    issues: list[ReviewIssuePayload]
    22→    assessments: dict[str, Any] | None
    23→    reviewed_files: list[str]
    24→
    25→
    26→def normalize_legacy_findings_alias(
    27→    payload: dict[str, Any],
    28→    *,
    29→    missing_issues_error: str,
    30→    allow_legacy_findings: bool = ALLOW_LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS,
    31→) -> str | None:
    32→    """Normalize legacy ``findings`` into canonical ``issues`` in one place.
    33→
    34→    ``allow_legacy_findings`` is the compatibility cutoff flag; once flipped to
    35→    ``False`` only canonical ``issues`` payloads are accepted.
    36→    """
    37→    if "issues" in payload:
    38→        return None
    39→    if "findings" not in payload:
    40→        return missing_issues_error
    41→    if not allow_legacy_findings:
    42→        return (
    43→            "legacy key 'findings' is no longer accepted; use 'issues' "
    44→            f"(support sunset: {LEGACY_FINDINGS_ALIAS_SUNSET_DATE})"
    45→        )
    46→    payload["issues"] = payload.pop("findings")
    47→    return None
    48→
    49→
    50→def extract_reviewed_files(data: list[dict] | dict) -> list[str]:
    51→    """Parse optional reviewed-file list from import payload."""
    52→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    53→        return []
    54→    raw = data.get("reviewed_files")
    55→    if not isinstance(raw, list):
    56→        return []
    57→
    58→    reviewed: list[str] = []
    59→    seen: set[str] = set()
    60→    for item in raw:
    61→        if not isinstance(item, str):
    62→            continue
    63→        path = item.strip()
    64→        if not path or path in seen:
    65→            continue
    66→        seen.add(path)
    67→        reviewed.append(path)
    68→    return reviewed
    69→
    70→
    71→def parse_review_import_payload(
    72→    data: ReviewImportPayload | dict[str, Any],
    73→    *,
    74→    mode_name: str,
    75→) -> ReviewImportEnvelope:
    76→    """Parse shared review import payload shape for per-file/holistic flows."""
    77→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
    78→        raise ValueError(f"{mode_name} review import payload must be a JSON object")
    79→
    80→    missing_issues_error = f"{mode_name} review import payload must contain 'issues'"
    81→    key_error = normalize_legacy_findings_alias(
    82→        data,
    83→        missing_issues_error=missing_issues_error,
    84→    )
    85→    if key_error is not None:
    86→        raise ValueError(key_error)
    87→
    88→    issues_list = data.get("issues")
    89→    if not isinstance(issues_list, list):
    90→        raise ValueError(f"{mode_name} review import payload 'issues' must be a list")
    91→    for idx, entry in enumerate(issues_list):
    92→        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
    93→            raise ValueError(
    94→                f"{mode_name} review import payload 'issues[{idx}]' must be an object"
    95→            )
    96→
    97→    assessments = data.get("assessments")
    98→    if assessments is not None and not isinstance(assessments, dict):
    99→        raise ValueError(
   100→            f"{mode_name} review import payload 'assessments' must be an object"
   101→        )
   102→    return ReviewImportEnvelope(
   103→        issues=issues_list,
   104→        assessments=assessments,
   105→        reviewed_files=extract_reviewed_files(data),
   106→    )
   107→
   108→
   109→def normalize_review_confidence(value: object) -> str:
   110→    """Normalize review confidence labels to high/medium/low."""
   111→    confidence = str(value).strip().lower()
   112→    return confidence if confidence in {"high", "medium", "low"} else "low"
   113→
   114→
   115→def review_tier(confidence: str, *, holistic: bool) -> int:
   116→    """Derive natural tier from review confidence and scope."""
   117→    if confidence == "high":
   118→        return 1 if holistic else 3
   119→    if confidence == "medium":
   120→        return 2 if holistic else 3
   121→    return 3
   122→

1→"""AST detectors that operate on function/class nodes."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import ast
     6→
     7→from desloppify.languages.python.detectors.smells_ast._helpers import (
     8→    _is_docstring,

    11→
    12→
    13→def _is_test_file(filepath: str) -> bool:
    14→    """Return True when a path clearly points to a test module."""
    15→    normalized = filepath.replace("\\", "/")
    16→    return normalized.startswith("tests/") or "/tests/" in normalized
    17→
    18→
    19→def _detect_monster_functions(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
    20→    """Flag functions longer than 150 LOC."""
    21→    if not (hasattr(node, "end_lineno") and node.end_lineno):
    22→        return []
    23→    loc = node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1
    24→    if loc > 150:
    25→        return [
    26→            {
    27→                "file": filepath,
    28→                "line": node.lineno,
    29→                "content": f"{node.name}() — {loc} LOC",
    30→            }
    31→        ]
    32→    return []
    33→
    34→
    35→def _detect_dead_functions(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
    36→    """Flag functions whose body is only pass, return, or return None."""
    37→    if node.decorator_list:
    38→        return []
    39→    body = node.body
    40→    if len(body) == 1:
    41→        stmt = body[0]
    42→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Pass) or _is_return_none(stmt):
    43→            return [
    44→                {
    45→                    "file": filepath,
    46→                    "line": node.lineno,
    47→                    "content": f"{node.name}() — body is only {ast.dump(stmt)[:40]}",
    48→                }
    49→            ]
    50→    elif len(body) == 2:
    51→        first, second = body
    52→        if not _is_docstring(first):
    53→            return []
    54→        if isinstance(second, ast.Pass):
    55→            desc = "docstring + pass"
    56→        elif _is_return_none(second):
    57→            desc = "docstring + return None"
    58→        else:
    59→            return []
    60→        return [
    61→            {
    62→                "file": filepath,
    63→                "line": node.lineno,
    64→                "content": f"{node.name}() — {desc}",
    65→            }
    66→        ]
    67→    return []
    68→
    69→
    70→def _detect_deferred_imports(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
    71→    """Flag function-level imports (possible circular import workarounds)."""
    72→    if _is_test_file(filepath):
    73→        return []
    74→    _SKIP_MODULES = ("typing", "typing_extensions", "__future__")
    75→    for child in ast.walk(node):
    76→        if (
    77→            not isinstance(child, ast.Import | ast.ImportFrom)
    78→            or child.lineno <= node.lineno
    79→        ):
    80→            continue
    81→        module = getattr(child, "module", None) or ""
    82→        if module in _SKIP_MODULES:
    83→            continue
    84→        names = ", ".join(a.name for a in child.names[:3])
    85→        if len(child.names) > 3:
    86→            names += f", +{len(child.names) - 3}"
    87→        return [
    88→            {
    89→                "file": filepath,
    90→                "line": child.lineno,
    91→                "content": f"import {module or names} inside {node.name}()",
    92→            }
    93→        ]
    94→    return []
    95→
    96→
    97→def _detect_inline_classes(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
    98→    """Flag classes defined inside functions."""
    99→    results: list[dict] = []
   100→    for child in node.body:
   101→        if isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef):
   102→            results.append(
   103→                {
   104→                    "file": filepath,
   105→                    "line": child.lineno,
   106→                    "content": f"class {child.name} defined inside {node.name}()",
   107→                }
   108→            )
   109→    return results
   110→
   111→
   112→_FUNC_TYPES = (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.Lambda)
   113→_BLOCK_ATTRS = ("body", "handlers", "orelse", "finalbody")
   114→
   115→
   116→def _walk_inner_defs(
   117→    body: list[ast.AST], depth: int, inner_defs: list[ast.AST],
   118→) -> int:
   119→    """Recursively collect inner function/lambda defs and return max nesting depth."""
   120→    max_depth = 0
   121→    for child in body:
   122→        if isinstance(child, _FUNC_TYPES):
   123→            inner_defs.append(child)
   124→            current_depth = depth + 1
   125→            max_depth = max(max_depth, current_depth)
   126→            child_body = getattr(child, "body", None)
   127→            if isinstance(child_body, list):
   128→                max_depth = max(
   129→                    max_depth,
   130→                    _walk_inner_defs(child_body, current_depth, inner_defs),
   131→                )
   132→            elif isinstance(child, ast.Lambda):
   133→                max_depth = max(
   134→                    max_depth,
   135→                    _collect_nested_lambdas(child, current_depth, inner_defs),
   136→                )
   137→        else:
   138→            for attr in _BLOCK_ATTRS:
   139→                sub_body = getattr(child, attr, None)
   140→                if isinstance(sub_body, list):
   141→                    max_depth = max(
   142→                        max_depth, _walk_inner_defs(sub_body, depth, inner_defs),
   143→                    )
   144→    return max_depth
   145→
   146→
   147→def _collect_nested_lambdas(
   148→    parent: ast.Lambda, depth: int, inner_defs: list[ast.AST],
   149→) -> int:
   150→    """Walk a lambda's expression body for nested lambdas."""
   151→    max_depth = depth
   152→    for sub in ast.walk(parent.body):
   153→        if isinstance(sub, ast.Lambda) and sub is not parent:
   154→            inner_defs.append(sub)
   155→            max_depth = max(max_depth, depth + 1)
   156→    return max_depth
   157→
   158→
   159→def _format_inner_def_names(inner_defs: list[ast.AST]) -> str:
   160→    """Format inner def names for the issue content string."""
   161→    names = [
   162→        getattr(d, "name", "<lambda>")
   163→        for d in inner_defs[:5]
   164→        if isinstance(d, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)
   165→    ]
   166→    names_str = ", ".join(names) if names else "<lambdas>"
   167→    if len(inner_defs) > 5:
   168→        names_str += ", ..."
   169→    return names_str
   170→
   171→
   172→def _detect_nested_closures(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
   173→    """Flag functions with deeply nested inner defs or too many inner defs total."""
   174→    inner_defs: list[ast.AST] = []
   175→    max_depth = _walk_inner_defs(node.body, 0, inner_defs)
   176→
   177→    if max_depth < 2 and len(inner_defs) < 3:
   178→        return []
   179→    return [
   180→        {
   181→            "file": filepath,
   182→            "line": node.lineno,
   183→            "content": (
   184→                f"{node.name}() — {len(inner_defs)} inner defs"
   185→                f" (depth {max_depth}): {_format_inner_def_names(inner_defs)}"
   186→            ),
   187→        }
   188→    ]
   189→
   190→
   191→def _collect_single_list_assignments(body: list[ast.AST]) -> dict[str, int]:
   192→    """Return {name: lineno} for `x = [single_value]` assignments."""
   193→    result: dict[str, int] = {}
   194→    for stmt in body:
   195→        if not isinstance(stmt, ast.Assign) or len(stmt.targets) != 1:
   196→            continue
   197→        target = stmt.targets[0]
   198→        if (
   199→            isinstance(target, ast.Name)
   200→            and isinstance(stmt.value, ast.List)
   201→            and len(stmt.value.elts) == 1
   202→        ):
   203→            result[target.id] = stmt.lineno
   204→    return result
   205→
   206→
   207→def _find_subscript_zero_refs(
   208→    node: ast.AST, candidate_names: set[str],
   209→) -> set[str]:
   210→    """Find names from candidate_names accessed as x[0] inside nested functions."""
   211→    used: set[str] = set()
   212→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   213→        if child is node or not isinstance(child, _FUNC_TYPES):
   214→            continue
   215→        for sub in ast.walk(child):
   216→            if not isinstance(sub, ast.Subscript):
   217→                continue
   218→            if not isinstance(sub.value, ast.Name):
   219→                continue
   220→            if sub.value.id not in candidate_names:
   221→                continue
   222→            if isinstance(sub.slice, ast.Constant) and sub.slice.value == 0:
   223→                used.add(sub.value.id)
   224→    return used
   225→
   226→
   227→def _detect_mutable_ref_hack(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
   228→    """Flag mutable-list-as-ref hacks: x = [value] then x[0] inside a nested function."""
   229→    single_list_names = _collect_single_list_assignments(node.body)
   230→    if not single_list_names:
   231→        return []
   232→
   233→    used_names = _find_subscript_zero_refs(node, set(single_list_names))
   234→    return [
   235→        {
   236→            "file": filepath,
   237→            "line": single_list_names[name],
   238→            "content": (
   239→                f"{name} = [v] in {node.name}()"
   240→                " — mutable-list ref hack (use nonlocal or a dataclass)"
   241→            ),
   242→        }
   243→        for name in sorted(used_names)
   244→    ]
   245→
   246→
   247→# Node types that contribute to cyclomatic complexity.
   248→_DECISION_TYPES = (
   249→    ast.If, ast.IfExp, ast.For, ast.AsyncFor, ast.While,
   250→    ast.ExceptHandler, ast.With, ast.AsyncWith, ast.Assert,
   251→)
   252→
   253→
   254→def _compute_cyclomatic_complexity(node: ast.AST) -> int:
   255→    """Compute cyclomatic complexity for a function AST node."""
   256→    complexity = 1
   257→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   258→        if isinstance(child, _DECISION_TYPES):
   259→            complexity += 1
   260→        elif isinstance(child, ast.BoolOp):
   261→            complexity += len(child.values) - 1
   262→    return complexity
   263→
   264→
   265→def _detect_high_cyclomatic_complexity(filepath: str, node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]:
   266→    """Flag functions with cyclomatic complexity > 12."""
   267→    complexity = _compute_cyclomatic_complexity(node)
   268→    if complexity > 12:
   269→        return [
   270→            {
   271→                "file": filepath,
   272→                "line": node.lineno,
   273→                "content": f"{node.name}() — cyclomatic complexity {complexity}",
   274→            }
   275→        ]
   276→    return []
   277→
   278→
   279→def _detect_lru_cache_mutable(
   280→    filepath: str,
   281→    node: ast.AST,
   282→    tree: ast.Module,
   283→) -> list[dict]:
   284→    """Flag @lru_cache/@cache functions that reference module-level mutable variables.
   285→
   286→    Finds globals referenced in the function body that aren't in the parameter list,
   287→    checking if those names are assigned to mutable values at module level.
   288→    """
   289→    # Check if this function has @lru_cache or @cache decorator
   290→    has_cache = False
   291→    for dec in node.decorator_list:
   292→        if isinstance(dec, ast.Name) and dec.id in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   293→            has_cache = True
   294→        elif isinstance(dec, ast.Call) and isinstance(dec.func, ast.Name):
   295→            if dec.func.id in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   296→                has_cache = True
   297→        elif isinstance(dec, ast.Attribute) and dec.attr in ("lru_cache", "cache"):
   298→            has_cache = True
   299→    if not has_cache:
   300→        return []
   301→
   302→    # Get parameter names
   303→    param_names = set()
   304→    for arg in node.args.args + node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   305→        param_names.add(arg.arg)
   306→    if node.args.vararg:
   307→        param_names.add(node.args.vararg.arg)
   308→    if node.args.kwarg:
   309→        param_names.add(node.args.kwarg.arg)
   310→
   311→    # Collect module-level mutable assignments
   312→    module_mutables = set()
   313→    for stmt in tree.body:
   314→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Assign):
   315→            for target in stmt.targets:
   316→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and isinstance(
   317→                    stmt.value, ast.List | ast.Dict | ast.Set | ast.Call
   318→                ):
   319→                    module_mutables.add(target.id)
   320→        elif (
   321→            isinstance(stmt, ast.AnnAssign)
   322→            and stmt.target
   323→            and isinstance(stmt.target, ast.Name)
   324→        ):
   325→            if stmt.value and isinstance(
   326→                stmt.value, ast.List | ast.Dict | ast.Set | ast.Call
   327→            ):
   328→                module_mutables.add(stmt.target.id)
   329→
   330→    # Find Name references in function body that point to module-level mutables
   331→    for child in ast.walk(node):
   332→        if (
   333→            isinstance(child, ast.Name)
   334→            and child.id in module_mutables
   335→            and child.id not in param_names
   336→        ):
   337→            return [
   338→                {
   339→                    "file": filepath,
   340→                    "line": node.lineno,
   341→                    "content": f"@lru_cache on {node.name}() reads mutable global '{child.id}'",
   342→                }
   343→            ]
   344→    return []
   345→

   417→        "Hey — organize is confirmed. Next: enrich your steps"
   418→        " with detail and issue_refs so they're executor-ready."
   419→        " Run `desloppify plan triage --stage enrich --report \"...\"`."
   420→        " You can still reorganize (add/remove clusters, reorder)"
   421→        " during the enrich stage."
   422→    )
   423→
   424→def _confirm_enrich(
   425→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   426→    plan: dict,
   427→    stages: dict,
   428→    attestation: str | None,
   429→    *,
   430→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   431→) -> None:
   432→    """Show enrich summary and record confirmation if attestation is valid."""
   433→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   434→    if "enrich" not in stages:
   435→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm: enrich stage not recorded.", "red"))
   436→        print(colorize('  Run: desloppify plan triage --stage enrich --report "..."', "dim"))
   437→        return
   438→    if stages["enrich"].get("confirmed_at"):
   439→        print(colorize("  Enrich stage already confirmed.", "green"))
   440→        return
   441→
   442→    from ._stage_validation import (
   443→        _shallow_steps,
   444→        _steps_missing_issue_refs,
   445→        _steps_referencing_skipped_issues,
   446→        _steps_with_bad_paths,
   447→        _steps_with_vague_detail,
   448→        _steps_without_effort,
   449→    )
   450→
   451→    print(colorize("  Stage: ENRICH — Make steps executor-ready (detail, refs)", "bold"))
   452→    print(colorize("  " + "─" * 54, "dim"))
   453→
   454→    shallow = _shallow_steps(plan)
   455→    if shallow:
   456→        total_bare = sum(n for _, n, _ in shallow)
   457→        print(colorize(f"  Cannot confirm: {total_bare} step(s) still lack detail or issue_refs.", "red"))
   458→        for name, bare, total in shallow[:5]:
   459→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {bare}/{total} steps", "yellow"))
   460→        print()
   461→        print(colorize("  Every step needs --detail (sub-points) or --issue-refs (for auto-completion).", "dim"))
   462→        print(colorize("  Fix:", "dim"))
   463→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   464→        return
   465→    else:
   466→        print(colorize("  All steps have detail or issue_refs.", "green"))
   467→
   468→    # Block on bad file paths at confirm time
   469→    from desloppify.base.discovery.paths import get_project_root
   470→    bad_paths = _steps_with_bad_paths(plan, get_project_root())
   471→    if bad_paths:
   472→        total_bad = sum(len(bp) for _, _, bp in bad_paths)
   473→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_bad} file path(s) in step details don't exist on disk.", "red"))
   474→        for name, step_num, paths in bad_paths:
   475→            for p in paths:
   476→                print(colorize(f"    {name} step {step_num}: {p}", "yellow"))
   477→        print(colorize("  Fix paths with: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --detail '...'", "dim"))
   478→        return
   479→
   480→    # Block on missing effort tags (was advisory, now blocking)
   481→    untagged = _steps_without_effort(plan)
   482→    if untagged:
   483→        total_missing = sum(n for _, n, _ in untagged)
   484→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_missing} step(s) have no effort tag.", "red"))
   485→        for name, missing, total in untagged[:5]:
   486→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {missing}/{total} steps missing effort", "yellow"))
   487→        print(colorize("  Every step needs --effort (trivial/small/medium/large).", "dim"))
   488→        print(colorize("  Fix: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --effort small", "dim"))
   489→        return
   490→
   491→    # Block on missing issue_refs (traceability)
   492→    no_refs = _steps_missing_issue_refs(plan)
   493→    if no_refs:
   494→        total_missing = sum(n for _, n, _ in no_refs)
   495→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {total_missing} step(s) have no issue_refs.", "red"))
   496→        for name, missing, total in no_refs[:5]:
   497→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: {missing}/{total} steps missing refs", "yellow"))
   498→        print(colorize("  Every step needs --issue-refs linking it to the review issue(s) it addresses.", "dim"))
   499→        print(colorize("  Fix: desloppify plan cluster update <name> --update-step N --issue-refs <hash1> <hash2>", "dim"))
   500→        return
   501→
   502→    # Block on vague detail (too short, no file paths)
   503→    vague = _steps_with_vague_detail(plan, get_project_root())
   504→    if vague:
   505→        print(colorize(f"\n  Cannot confirm: {len(vague)} step(s) have vague detail (< 80 chars, no file paths).", "red"))
   506→        for name, step_num, title in vague[:5]:
   507→            print(colorize(f"    {name} step {step_num}: {title}", "yellow"))
   508→        print(colorize("  Executor-ready means: someone with zero context knows which file to open and what to change.", "dim"))
   509→        print(colorize("  Add file paths and specific instructions to each step's --detail.", "dim"))
   510→        return
   511→
   512→    # Warn on steps referencing skipped/wontfixed issues
   513→    stale_refs = _steps_referencing_skipped_issues(plan)
   514→    if stale_refs:
   515→        total_stale = sum(len(ids) for _, _, ids in stale_refs)
   516→        print(colorize(f"\n  Warning: {total_stale} step issue_ref(s) point to skipped/wontfixed issues.", "yellow"))
   517→        for name, step_num, ids in stale_refs[:5]:
   518→            print(colorize(f"    {name} step {step_num}: {', '.join(ids[:3])}", "yellow"))
   519→        print(colorize("  Consider removing stale refs or removing the step if it's no longer needed.", "dim"))
   520→
   521→    enrich_clusters = [n for n in plan.get("clusters", {}) if not plan["clusters"][n].get("auto")]
   522→
   523→    if not attestation or len(attestation.strip()) < _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN:
   524→        if attestation:
   525→            print(colorize(
   526→                f"\n  Attestation too short ({len(attestation.strip())} chars, min {_MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN}).",
   527→                "red",
   528→            ))
   529→        print(colorize("\n  If satisfied, confirm:", "dim"))
   530→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan triage --confirm enrich --attestation "Steps are executor-ready..."', "dim"))
   531→        return
   532→
   533→    validation_err = _validate_attestation(
   534→        attestation.strip(), "enrich", cluster_names=enrich_clusters,
   535→    )
   536→    if validation_err:
   537→        print(colorize(f"\n  {validation_err}", "red"))
   538→        return
   539→
   540→    stages["enrich"]["confirmed_at"] = utc_now()
   541→    stages["enrich"]["confirmed_text"] = attestation.strip()
   542→    purge_triage_stage(plan, "enrich")
   543→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   544→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   545→        plan,
   546→        "triage_confirm_enrich",
   547→        actor="user",
   548→        detail={"attestation": attestation.strip()},
   549→    )
   550→    resolved_services.save_plan(plan)
   551→    print(colorize(f'  ✓ Enrich confirmed: "{attestation.strip()}"', "green"))
   552→    print_user_message(
   553→        "Hey — enrich is confirmed. Run `desloppify plan triage"
   554→        " --complete --strategy \"...\"` to finish triage."
   555→    )
   556→
   557→
   558→def _cmd_confirm_stage(
   559→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   560→    *,
   561→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   562→) -> None:
   563→    """Router for ``--confirm observe/reflect/organize/enrich``."""
   564→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   565→    confirm_stage = getattr(args, "confirm", None)
   566→    attestation = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
   567→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   568→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   569→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   570→
   571→    if confirm_stage == "observe":
   572→        _confirm_observe(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   573→    elif confirm_stage == "reflect":
   574→        _confirm_reflect(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   575→    elif confirm_stage == "organize":
   576→        _confirm_organize(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   577→    elif confirm_stage == "enrich":
   578→        _confirm_enrich(args, plan, stages, attestation, services=resolved_services)
   579→
   580→
   581→MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN = _MIN_ATTESTATION_LEN
   582→validate_attestation = _validate_attestation
   583→
   584→
   585→def cmd_confirm_stage(
   586→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   587→    *,
   588→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   589→) -> None:

     5→
     6→def parse_dimensions(args: object) -> set[str] | None:
     7→    """Parse ``--dimensions`` from *args* into a set, or ``None`` if absent."""
     8→    raw = getattr(args, "dimensions", None)
     9→    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():
    10→        return None
    11→    return {d.strip() for d in raw.split(",") if d.strip()}

1→"""Stale @deprecated symbol detection."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import json
     6→import logging
     7→import re
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→from typing import Any
    10→
    11→from desloppify.base.discovery.file_paths import (
    12→
    13→    rel,
    14→
    15→    resolve_path,
    16→
    17→)
    18→
    19→from desloppify.base.discovery.source import find_ts_files
    20→from desloppify.base.output.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    21→from desloppify.base.search.grep import grep_count_files, grep_files
    22→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize, print_table
    23→from desloppify.base.signal_patterns import DEPRECATION_MARKER_RE
    24→from desloppify.languages.typescript.detectors.contracts import DetectorResult
    25→
    26→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    27→def detect_deprecated_result(path: Path) -> DetectorResult[dict[str, Any]]:
    28→    """Find deprecated symbols with explicit population semantics."""
    29→    ts_files = find_ts_files(path)
    30→    hits = grep_files(DEPRECATION_MARKER_RE.pattern, ts_files, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    31→
    32→    entries = []
    33→    seen_symbols = set()  # Deduplicate by file+symbol
    34→    for filepath, lineno, content in hits:
    35→        symbol, kind = _extract_deprecated_symbol(
    36→            filepath,
    37→            lineno,
    38→            content,
    39→            scan_root=path,
    40→        )
    41→        if not symbol:
    42→            continue
    43→        # Deduplicate (same symbol in same file, e.g., multiple @deprecated on interface props)
    44→        key = (filepath, symbol)
    45→        if key in seen_symbols:
    46→            continue
    47→        seen_symbols.add(key)
    48→        importers = (
    49→            _count_importers(symbol, filepath, ts_files=ts_files, scan_root=path)
    50→            if kind == "top-level"
    51→            else -1
    52→        )
    53→        entries.append(
    54→            {
    55→                "file": filepath,
    56→                "line": lineno,
    57→                "symbol": symbol,
    58→                "kind": kind,
    59→                "importers": importers,
    60→            }
    61→        )
    62→    sorted_entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e["importers"])
    63→    return DetectorResult(
    64→        entries=sorted_entries,
    65→        population_kind="deprecated_symbols",
    66→        population_size=len(sorted_entries),
    67→    )
    68→
    69→
    70→def _extract_deprecated_symbol(
    71→    filepath: str,
    72→    lineno: int,
    73→    content: str,
    74→    *,
    75→    scan_root: Path | None = None,
    76→) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    77→    """Extract the deprecated symbol name and whether it's a top-level or inline deprecation.
    78→
    79→    Returns (symbol_name, kind) where kind is "top-level" or "property".
    80→    """
    81→    try:
    82→        p = _resolve_source_file(filepath, scan_root=scan_root)
    83→        lines = p.read_text().splitlines()
    84→        content_stripped = content.strip()
    85→
    86→        # Case 1: Inline @deprecated on a property/field
    87→        # e.g., `/** @deprecated Use X instead */ fieldName?: Type;`
    88→        # or `/** @deprecated */ export const oldThing = ...`
    89→        if "/**" in content_stripped and "*/" in content_stripped:
    90→            # This is a single-line JSDoc. Check what follows on the same or next line
    91→            after_jsdoc = content_stripped.split("*/", 1)[1].strip()
    92→            if after_jsdoc:
    93→                # Property on same line: `/** @deprecated */ someField?: string;`
    94→                m = re.match(r"(\w+)\s*[?:=]", after_jsdoc)
    95→                if m:
    96→                    return m.group(1), "property"
    97→                # Declaration on same line: `/** @deprecated */ export const foo`
    98→                m = re.match(
    99→                    r"(?:export\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function|class|type|interface|enum)\s+(\w+)",
   100→                    after_jsdoc,
   101→                )
   102→                if m:
   103→                    return m.group(1), "top-level"
   104→
   105→        # Case 2: @deprecated inside a multi-line JSDoc block — check if it's on a property
   106→        # We need to look ahead to find what this annotates
   107→        for offset in range(1, 8):
   108→            idx = lineno - 1 + offset
   109→            if idx >= len(lines):
   110→                break
   111→            src = lines[idx].strip()
   112→            # Skip empty lines, comment continuations, closing comment
   113→            if not src or src.startswith("*") or src.startswith("//"):
   114→                continue
   115→            # Top-level declaration
   116→            m = re.match(
   117→                r"(?:export\s+)?(?:declare\s+)?(?:const|let|var|function|class|type|interface|enum)\s+(\w+)",
   118→                src,
   119→            )
   120→            if m:
   121→                return m.group(1), "top-level"
   122→            # Property/field: `fieldName?: Type;` or `fieldName: Type;`
   123→            m = re.match(r"(\w+)\s*[?:]", src)
   124→            if m:
   125→                return m.group(1), "property"
   126→            break
   127→
   128→        # Case 3: @deprecated as inline comment on same line
   129→        # e.g., `shotImageEntryId?: string; // @deprecated`
   130→        # Check the current line for a preceding field name
   131→        if "//" in content_stripped or "*" in content_stripped:
   132→            # Look at the same line before the @deprecated
   133→            marker_match = re.search(r"@deprecated", content_stripped, re.IGNORECASE)
   134→            line_before = content_stripped
   135→            if marker_match:
   136→                line_before = content_stripped[: marker_match.start()]
   137→            line_before = line_before.strip().rstrip("/*").rstrip("*").strip()
   138→            m = re.search(r"(\w+)\s*[?:]", line_before)
   139→            if m:
   140→                return m.group(1), "property"
   141→
   142→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   143→        log_best_effort_failure(
   144→            logger, f"read deprecated source context {filepath}", exc
   145→        )
   146→    return None, "unknown"
   147→
   148→
   149→def _resolve_source_file(filepath: str, *, scan_root: Path | None) -> Path:
   150→    if Path(filepath).is_absolute():
   151→        return Path(filepath)
   152→    if scan_root is not None:
   153→        candidate = scan_root / filepath
   154→        if candidate.exists():
   155→            return candidate
   156→    return Path(resolve_path(filepath))
   157→
   158→
   159→def _count_importers(
   160→    name: str, declaring_file: str, *, ts_files: list[str], scan_root: Path
   161→) -> int:
   162→    if not name:
   163→        return -1
   164→    matching = grep_count_files(name, ts_files, word_boundary=True)
   165→    declaring_resolved = str(
   166→        _resolve_source_file(declaring_file, scan_root=scan_root).resolve()
   167→    )
   168→    count = 0
   169→    for match_file in matching:
   170→        match_resolved = str(_resolve_source_file(match_file, scan_root=scan_root).resolve())
   171→        if match_resolved != declaring_resolved:
   172→            count += 1
   173→    return count
   174→
   175→
   176→def cmd_deprecated(args: Any) -> None:
   177→    result = detect_deprecated_result(Path(args.path))
   178→    entries = result.entries
   179→    if args.json:
   180→        print(
   181→            json.dumps(
   182→                {
   183→                    "count": len(entries),
   184→                    "entries": entries,
   185→                    "population_size": result.population_size,
   186→                },
   187→                indent=2,
   188→            )
   189→        )
   190→        return
   191→
   192→    if not entries:
   193→        print(colorize("No @deprecated annotations found.", "green"))
   194→        return
   195→
   196→    # Separate top-level and property deprecations
   197→    top_level = [e for e in entries if e["kind"] == "top-level"]
   198→    properties = [e for e in entries if e["kind"] == "property"]
   199→
   200→    print(
   201→        colorize(
   202→            f"\nDeprecated symbols: {len(entries)} ({len(top_level)} top-level, {len(properties)} properties)\n",
   203→            "bold",
   204→        )
   205→    )
   206→
   207→    if top_level:
   208→        print(colorize("Top-level (importable):", "cyan"))
   209→        rows = []
   210→        for e in top_level[: args.top]:
   211→            imp = str(e["importers"]) if e["importers"] >= 0 else "?"
   212→            status = (
   213→                colorize("safe to remove", "green")
   214→                if e["importers"] == 0
   215→                else f"{imp} importers"
   216→            )
   217→            rows.append([e["symbol"], rel(e["file"]), status])
   218→        print_table(["Symbol", "File", "Status"], rows, [30, 55, 20])
   219→        print()
   220→
   221→    if properties:
   222→        print(colorize("Properties (inline):", "cyan"))
   223→        rows = []
   224→        for e in properties[: args.top]:
   225→            rows.append([e["symbol"], rel(e["file"]), f"line {e['line']}"])
   226→        print_table(["Property", "File", "Line"], rows, [30, 55, 10])
   227→

    20→def _front_item_ids(front_item: dict) -> tuple[str, set[str]]:
    21→    front_id = front_item["id"]
    22→    front_ids = {front_id}
    23→    if front_item.get("kind") != "cluster":
    24→        return front_id, front_ids
    25→    for member in front_item.get("members", []):

    30→def _resolve_target_ids(patterns: list[str], clusters: dict) -> set[str]:
    31→    resolved_ids: set[str] = set()
    32→    for pattern in patterns:
    33→        if pattern in clusters:
    34→            resolved_ids.update(clusters[pattern].get("issue_ids", []))
    35→            resolved_ids.add(pattern)
    36→            continue
    37→        resolved_ids.add(pattern)
    38→    return resolved_ids

    42→    resolved_ids: set[str],
    43→    *,
    44→    clusters: dict,
    45→    issues: dict,
    46→) -> set[str]:
    47→    return {
    48→        issue_id
    49→        for issue_id in resolved_ids
    50→        if issue_id in clusters
    51→        or (issue_id in issues and issues[issue_id].get("status") == "open")
    52→    }

    54→
    55→def _prune_front_covered_clusters(
    56→    out_of_order: set[str],
    57→    *,
    58→    clusters: dict,
    59→    issues: dict,
    60→    front_ids: set[str],
    61→) -> None:
    62→    for cluster_id in list(out_of_order):

    64→            continue
    65→        alive_members = {
    66→            issue_id
    67→            for issue_id in clusters[cluster_id].get("issue_ids", [])
    68→            if issue_id in issues and issues[issue_id].get("status") == "open"
    69→        }

    84→
    85→def _check_queue_order_guard(
    86→    state: dict,
    87→    patterns: list[str],
    88→    status: str,
    89→) -> bool:
    90→    """Warn and block if resolving items not at the front of the plan queue."""
    91→    if status != "fixed":
    92→        return False
    93→    try:
    94→        if not has_living_plan():
    95→            return False
    96→        plan = load_plan()
    97→        queue_order = plan.get("queue_order", [])
    98→        if not queue_order:
    99→            return False
   100→
   101→        ctx = queue_context(state, plan=plan)
   102→        result = build_work_queue(
   103→            state,
   104→            options=QueueBuildOptions(
   105→                count=None,
   106→                include_subjective=True,
   107→                context=ctx,
   108→            ),
   109→        )
   110→        items = result["items"]
   111→        if not plan.get("active_cluster"):
   112→            items = collapse_clusters(items, plan)
   113→        if not items:
   114→            return False
   115→
   116→        clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   117→        issues = state.get("issues", {})
   118→        resolved_ids = _resolve_target_ids(patterns, clusters)
   119→        resolved_ids = _filter_open_or_cluster_targets(
   120→            resolved_ids,
   121→            clusters=clusters,
   122→            issues=issues,
   123→        )
   124→        if not resolved_ids:
   125→            return False
   126→
   127→        # Collect IDs from the first N queue positions where N is the
   128→        # number of items being resolved.  This allows batch-resolving
   129→        # a contiguous prefix (e.g. the first 9 items in one command).
   130→        prefix_depth = max(len(resolved_ids), 1)
   131→        front_ids: set[str] = set()
   132→        front_id = items[0]["id"]
   133→        for item in items[:prefix_depth]:
   134→            _, item_ids = _front_item_ids(item)
   135→            front_ids.update(item_ids)
   136→
   137→        out_of_order = resolved_ids - front_ids
   138→        _prune_front_covered_clusters(
   139→            out_of_order,
   140→            clusters=clusters,
   141→            issues=issues,
   142→            front_ids=front_ids,
   143→        )
   144→        if not out_of_order:
   145→            return False
   146→
   147→        _print_queue_order_violation(front_id, out_of_order)
   148→        return True
   149→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   150→        _logger.debug("queue order guard skipped", exc_info=True)
   151→        return False
   152→
   153→
   154→__all__ = ["_check_queue_order_guard"]
   155→

     3→from __future__ import annotations
