    98→    if not isinstance(lang_name, str):
    99→        return None
   100→    cleaned = lang_name.strip().lower()
   101→    return cleaned or None
   102→
   103→
   104→def _merge_prompt_display_and_weights(
   105→    payload: dict[str, object],
   106→    *,
   107→    prompt_meta: dict[str, object],
   108→    override_existing: bool,
   109→) -> None:
   110→    if "display_name" in prompt_meta and (
   111→        override_existing or "display_name" not in payload
   112→    ):
   113→        payload["display_name"] = prompt_meta["display_name"]
   114→    if "weight" in prompt_meta and (override_existing or "weight" not in payload):
   115→        payload["weight"] = prompt_meta["weight"]
   116→    if "reset_on_scan" in prompt_meta and (
   117→        override_existing or "reset_on_scan" not in payload
   118→    ):
   119→        payload["reset_on_scan"] = prompt_meta["reset_on_scan"]
   120→
   121→
   122→def _merge_enabled_by_default_flag(
   123→    payload: dict[str, object],
   124→    *,
   125→    prompt_meta: dict[str, object],
   126→    override_existing: bool,
   127→    default_enabled: bool,
   128→) -> None:
   129→    if default_enabled:
   130→        payload["enabled_by_default"] = True
   131→    if "enabled_by_default" not in prompt_meta:
   132→        return
   133→    prompt_enabled = bool(prompt_meta["enabled_by_default"])
   134→    if override_existing:
   135→        payload["enabled_by_default"] = prompt_enabled
   136→        return
   137→    payload["enabled_by_default"] = bool(
   138→        payload.get("enabled_by_default", False) or prompt_enabled
   139→    )
   140→
   141→
   142→def _normalized_default_dimensions(dimensions: list[str]) -> set[str]:
   143→    return {
   144→        _normalize_dimension_name(dim)
   145→        for dim in dimensions
   146→        if isinstance(dim, str) and dim.strip()
   147→    }
   148→
   149→
   150→def _merge_dimension_meta(
   151→    target: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   152→    *,
   153→    dimensions: list[str],
   154→    prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]],
   155→    override_existing: bool = False,
   156→) -> None:
   157→    defaults = _normalized_default_dimensions(dimensions)
   158→
   159→    for raw_dim, entry in prompts.items():
   160→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw_dim)
   161→        if not dim:
   162→            continue
   163→
   164→        payload = target.setdefault(dim, {})
   165→        prompt_meta = extract_prompt_meta(entry)
   166→        _merge_prompt_display_and_weights(
   167→            payload,
   168→            prompt_meta=prompt_meta,
   169→            override_existing=override_existing,
   170→        )
   171→        _merge_enabled_by_default_flag(
   172→            payload,
   173→            prompt_meta=prompt_meta,
   174→            override_existing=override_existing,
   175→            default_enabled=dim in defaults,
   176→        )
   177→
   178→
   179→def _default_available_languages() -> list[str]:
   180→    try:
   181→        return list(_available_langs())
   182→    except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError):
   183→        return []
   184→
   185→
   186→def _default_load_dimensions_payload() -> tuple[
   187→    list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str
   188→]:
   189→    return _load_dimensions()
   190→
   191→
   192→def _default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(
   193→    lang_name: str,
   194→) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   195→    return _load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)
   196→
   197→
   198→class _SubjectiveProviderState:
   199→    def __init__(self) -> None:
   200→        self.available_languages_provider: Callable[[], list[str]] = (
   201→            _default_available_languages
   202→        )
   203→        self.load_dimensions_payload_provider: Callable[
   204→            [], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   205→        ] = _default_load_dimensions_payload
   206→        self.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider: Callable[
   207→            [str], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   208→        ] = _default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang
   209→
   210→
   211→_PROVIDER_STATE = _SubjectiveProviderState()
   212→
   213→
   214→def _available_languages() -> list[str]:
   215→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.available_languages_provider()
   216→
   217→
   218→def _load_dimensions_payload() -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   219→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.load_dimensions_payload_provider()
   220→
   221→
   222→def _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(
   223→    lang_name: str,
   224→) -> tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]:
   225→    return _PROVIDER_STATE.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider(lang_name)
   226→
   227→
   228→def _clear_subjective_dimension_caches() -> None:
   229→    default_dimension_keys.cache_clear()
   230→    default_dimension_keys_for_lang.cache_clear()
   231→    load_subjective_dimension_metadata.cache_clear()
   232→    load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang.cache_clear()
   233→
   234→
   235→def configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   236→    *,
   237→    available_languages_provider: Callable[[], list[str]] | None = None,
   238→    load_dimensions_payload_provider: Callable[
   239→        [], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   240→    ]
   241→    | None = None,
   242→    load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider: Callable[
   243→        [str], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   244→    ]
   245→    | None = None,
   246→) -> None:
   247→    """Configure metadata providers for subjective-dimension lookups."""
   248→    state = _PROVIDER_STATE
   249→
   250→    changed = False
   251→    if (
   252→        available_languages_provider is not None
   253→        and available_languages_provider is not state.available_languages_provider
   254→    ):
   255→        state.available_languages_provider = available_languages_provider
   256→        changed = True
   257→    if (
   258→        load_dimensions_payload_provider is not None
   259→        and load_dimensions_payload_provider
   260→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_provider
   261→    ):
   262→        state.load_dimensions_payload_provider = load_dimensions_payload_provider
   263→        changed = True
   264→    if (
   265→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider is not None
   266→        and load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   267→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   268→    ):
   269→        state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider = (
   270→            load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   271→        )
   272→        changed = True
   273→
   274→    if changed:
   275→        _clear_subjective_dimension_caches()
   276→
   277→
   278→def reset_subjective_dimension_providers() -> None:
   279→    """Reset metadata providers to built-in defaults."""
   280→    configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   281→        available_languages_provider=_default_available_languages,
   282→        load_dimensions_payload_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload,
   283→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider=_default_load_dimensions_payload_for_lang,
   284→    )
   285→
   286→
   287→def _normalize_dimension_list(values: list[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   288→    normalized: list[str] = []
   289→    for raw in values:
   290→        if not isinstance(raw, str):
   291→            continue
   292→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw)
   293→        if not dim or dim in normalized:
   294→            continue
   295→        normalized.append(dim)
   296→    return tuple(normalized)
   297→
   298→
   299→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   300→def default_dimension_keys() -> tuple[str, ...]:
   301→    """Return canonical default subjective dimension keys."""
   302→    try:
   303→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   304→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   305→        logger.debug("Failed to load default subjective dimensions: %s", exc)
   306→        return tuple(_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.keys())
   307→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   308→
   309→
   310→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   311→def default_dimension_keys_for_lang(lang_name: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   312→    """Return default subjective dimension keys for a specific language."""
   313→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   314→    if normalized is None:
   315→        return default_dimension_keys()
   316→    try:
   317→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(normalized)
   318→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   319→        logger.debug(
   320→            "Failed to load subjective dimensions for lang %s: %s",
   321→            normalized,
   322→            exc,
   323→        )
   324→        return default_dimension_keys()
   325→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)
   326→
   327→
   328→def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
   329→    *,
   330→    lang_name: str | None,
   331→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   332→    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   333→
   334→    try:
   335→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   336→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   337→        logger.debug("Failed to load shared subjective dimension payload: %s", exc)
   338→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts = [], {}
   339→    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)
   340→
   341→    langs = (
   342→        [lang_name]
   343→        if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip()
   344→        else _available_languages()
   345→    )
   346→    for name in langs:
   347→        try:
   348→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
   349→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   350→                out,
   351→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   352→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   353→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   354→            )
   355→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   356→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   357→            continue
   358→
   359→    for dim, payload in out.items():
   360→        payload.setdefault(
   361→            "display_name",
   362→            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
   363→        )
   364→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   365→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   366→        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
   367→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   368→        else:
   369→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   370→
   371→    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
   372→    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   373→        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
   374→        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
   375→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   376→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
   377→        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   378→
   379→    return out
   380→
   381→
   382→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   383→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   384→    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
   385→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)
   386→
   387→
   388→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   389→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
   390→    lang_name: str | None,
   391→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   392→    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
   393→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   394→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)
   395→
   396→
   397→def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   398→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   399→    if normalized is None:
   400→        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
   401→    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)
   402→
   403→
   404→def get_dimension_metadata(
   405→    dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None
   406→) -> dict[str, object]:
   407→    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
   408→    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
   409→    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
   410→    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))
   411→
   412→    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
   413→    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
   414→    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   415→    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   416→    return payload
   417→
   418→
   419→def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
   420→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   421→    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))
   422→
   423→
   424→def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
   425→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   426→    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
   427→    if is_numeric(raw):
   428→        return max(0.0, float(raw))
   429→    return 1.0
   430→
   431→
   432→def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
   433→    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
   434→    out: dict[str, str] = {}
   435→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   436→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   437→            continue
   438→        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
   439→    return out
   440→
   441→
   442→def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   443→    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
   444→    out = []
   445→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   446→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   447→            continue
   448→        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
   449→            continue
   450→        out.append(dim)
   451→    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))
   452→

    37→def _suggest_close_matches(state: dict, plan: dict | None, patterns: list[str]) -> None:
    38→    """Print fuzzy match suggestions for patterns that resolved to zero issues."""
    39→    all_ids: list[str] = list(state.get("issues", {}).keys())
    40→    if plan is not None:
    41→        seen_ids: set[str] = set(all_ids)
    42→        for fid in plan.get("queue_order", []):
    43→            if fid not in seen_ids:
    44→                seen_ids.add(fid)
    45→                all_ids.append(fid)
    46→        for cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).values():
    47→            for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", []):
    48→                if fid not in seen_ids:
    49→                    seen_ids.add(fid)
    50→                    all_ids.append(fid)
    51→
    52→    for pattern in patterns:
    53→        segments = pattern.split("::")
    54→        last_seg = segments[-1]
    55→        suggestions: list[str] = []
    56→
    57→        if _HEX8_RE.match(last_seg):
    58→            suggestions = [fid for fid in all_ids if fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}") or fid == last_seg]
    59→            if suggestions:
    60→                print(colorize(f"  No match for: {pattern!r}", "yellow"))
    61→                print(colorize("  Did you mean:", "dim"))
    62→                for m in suggestions[:3]:
    63→                    print(colorize(f"    {m}", "dim"))
    64→                print(colorize(f"  Tip: match by hash suffix alone: {last_seg}", "dim"))
    65→            continue
    66→

    68→        slug = segments[-2] if len(segments) >= 2 else ""
    69→        for fid in all_ids:
    70→            if f"::{last_seg}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{last_seg}"):

    72→            elif slug and (f"::{slug}::" in fid or fid.endswith(f"::{slug}")):

   138→
   139→    plan = load_plan()
   140→    issue_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, patterns, plan=plan)
   141→    if not issue_ids:
   142→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found.", "yellow"))
   143→        _print_pattern_hints()
   144→        _suggest_close_matches(state, plan, patterns)
   145→        return
   146→
   147→    if dry_run:
   148→        print(colorize(f"  [dry-run] Would add {len(issue_ids)} item(s) to {cluster_name}:", "cyan"))
   149→        for fid in issue_ids:
   150→            print(colorize(f"    {fid}", "dim"))
   151→        return
   152→
   153→    try:
   154→        count = add_to_cluster(plan, cluster_name, issue_ids)
   155→    except ValueError as ex:
   156→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   157→        return
   158→
   159→    # Check for overlap with other manual clusters
   160→    member_set = set(issue_ids)
   161→    for other_name, other_cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
   162→        if other_name == cluster_name or other_cluster.get("auto"):
   163→            continue
   164→        other_ids = set(other_cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   165→        if not other_ids:
   166→            continue
   167→        overlap = member_set & other_ids
   168→        if len(overlap) > len(other_ids) * 0.5:
   169→            print(colorize(
   170→                f"  Warning: {len(overlap)} issue(s) also in cluster '{other_name}' "
   171→                f"({len(overlap)}/{len(other_ids)} = {int(len(overlap)/len(other_ids)*100)}% overlap).",
   172→                "yellow",
   173→            ))
   174→
   175→    append_log_entry(
   176→        plan, "cluster_add", issue_ids=issue_ids, cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   177→    )
   178→    save_plan(plan)
   179→    print(colorize(f"  Added {count} item(s) to cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   180→

   232→def _resolve_item_position(
   233→    position: str,
   234→    target: str | None,
   235→    item_ids: list[str],
   236→    ordered_slice: list[str],
   237→    cluster_member_set: set[str],
   238→    cluster_name: str,
   239→    state: dict,
   240→    plan: dict,
   241→) -> tuple[str, str | None, int | None] | None:
   242→    """Resolve where items should be positioned within a cluster.
   243→
   244→    Returns (resolved_position, resolved_target, offset) on success,
   245→    or None if an error was printed and the caller should abort.
   246→    """
   247→    item_set = set(item_ids)
   248→
   249→    if position == "top":
   250→        first_non_item = next((fid for fid in ordered_slice if fid not in item_set), None)
   251→        if first_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[:len(item_ids)]) == item_set:
   252→            print(colorize("  Already at the top of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   253→            return None
   254→        return ("before", first_non_item, None)
   255→
   256→    if position == "bottom":
   257→        last_non_item = next((fid for fid in reversed(ordered_slice) if fid not in item_set), None)
   258→        if last_non_item is None or set(ordered_slice[-len(item_ids):]) == item_set:
   259→            print(colorize("  Already at the bottom of the cluster.", "yellow"))
   260→            return None
   261→        return ("after", last_non_item, None)
   262→
   263→    if position in ("before", "after"):
   264→        if target is None:
   265→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires a target. Example: --item PAT {position} TARGET", "red"))
   266→            return None
   267→        target_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [target], plan=plan)
   268→        if not target_ids:
   269→            print(colorize(f"  No match for target {target!r}.", "yellow"))
   270→            return None
   271→        resolved_target = target_ids[0]
   272→        if resolved_target not in cluster_member_set:
   273→            print(colorize(f"  Target {resolved_target!r} is not in cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   274→            return None
   275→        return (position, resolved_target, None)
   276→
   277→    if position in ("up", "down"):
   278→        if target is None:
   279→            print(colorize(f"  '{position}' requires an offset. Example: --item PAT {position} 3", "red"))
   280→            return None
   281→        try:
   282→            offset = int(target)
   283→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   284→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   285→            return None
   286→        return (position, None, offset)
   287→
   288→    return (position, None, None)
   289→
   290→
   291→def _reorder_within_cluster(
   292→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   293→    plan: dict,
   294→    clusters: dict,
   295→    cluster_names: list[str],
   296→    position: str,
   297→    target: str | None,
   298→    item_pattern: str,
   299→) -> None:
   300→    """Reorder items within a single cluster."""
   301→    if len(cluster_names) != 1:
   302→        print(colorize("  --item requires exactly one cluster name.", "red"))
   303→        return
   304→    cluster_name = cluster_names[0]
   305→    cluster_member_set = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids", []))
   306→
   307→    state = command_runtime(args).state
   308→    item_ids = resolve_ids_from_patterns(state, [item_pattern], plan=plan)
   309→    if not item_ids:
   310→        print(colorize("  No matching issues found for --item pattern.", "yellow"))
   311→        return
   312→    for fid in item_ids:
   313→        if fid not in cluster_member_set:
   314→            print(colorize(f"  {fid!r} is not a member of cluster {cluster_name!r}.", "red"))
   315→            return
   316→
   317→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   318→    ordered_slice = [fid for fid in queue_order if fid in cluster_member_set]
   319→
   320→    result = _resolve_item_position(
   321→        position, target, item_ids, ordered_slice,
   322→        cluster_member_set, cluster_name, state, plan,
   323→    )
   324→    if result is None:
   325→        return
   326→    resolved_position, resolved_target, offset = result
   327→
   328→    count = move_items(plan, item_ids, resolved_position, target=resolved_target, offset=offset)
   329→    append_log_entry(
   330→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=cluster_name, actor="user",
   331→        detail={"position": resolved_position, "count": count, "item": item_pattern},
   332→    )
   333→    save_plan(plan)
   334→    print(colorize(f"  Moved {count} item(s) to {resolved_position} within cluster {cluster_name}.", "green"))
   335→
   336→
   337→def _reorder_whole_clusters(
   338→    plan: dict,
   339→    clusters: dict,
   340→    cluster_names: list[str],
   341→    position: str,
   342→    target: str | None,
   343→) -> None:
   344→    """Reorder entire clusters as blocks relative to each other."""
   345→    target = resolve_target(plan, target, position)
   346→
   347→    offset = None
   348→    if position in ("up", "down") and target is not None:
   349→        try:
   350→            offset = int(target)
   351→        except (ValueError, TypeError):
   352→            print(colorize(f"  Invalid offset: {target}", "red"))
   353→            return
   354→        target = None
   355→
   356→    seen: set[str] = set()
   357→    all_member_ids: list[str] = []
   358→    for name in cluster_names:
   359→        for fid in clusters[name].get("issue_ids", []):
   360→            if fid not in seen:
   361→                seen.add(fid)
   362→                all_member_ids.append(fid)
   363→
   364→    if not all_member_ids:
   365→        print(colorize("  No members in the specified cluster(s).", "yellow"))
   366→        return
   367→
   368→    count = move_items(plan, all_member_ids, position, target=target, offset=offset)
   369→    append_log_entry(
   370→        plan, "cluster_reorder", cluster_name=",".join(cluster_names), actor="user",
   371→        detail={"position": position, "count": count},
   372→    )
   373→    save_plan(plan)
   374→    label = ", ".join(cluster_names)
   375→    print(colorize(f"  Moved cluster(s) {label} ({count} items) to {position}.", "green"))
   376→
   377→
   378→def _cmd_cluster_reorder(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   379→    raw_names: str = getattr(args, "cluster_names", "") or getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   380→    cluster_names: list[str] = [n.strip() for n in raw_names.split(",") if n.strip()]
   381→    position: str = getattr(args, "position", "top")
   382→    target: str | None = getattr(args, "target", None)
   383→    item_pattern: str | None = getattr(args, "item_pattern", None)
   384→
   385→    plan = load_plan()
   386→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   387→
   388→    # Validate all names exist
   389→    for name in cluster_names:
   390→        if name not in clusters:
   391→            print(colorize(f"  Cluster {name!r} does not exist.", "red"))
   392→            return
   393→
   394→    if item_pattern is not None:
   395→        _reorder_within_cluster(args, plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target, item_pattern)
   396→    else:
   397→        _reorder_whole_clusters(plan, clusters, cluster_names, position, target)

   421→def _print_step(i: int, step: str | dict) -> None:
   422→    """Print a single step with title, detail, refs, and done status."""
   423→    if isinstance(step, str):
   424→        print(colorize(f"    {i}. {step}", "dim"))
   425→        return
   426→    done = step.get("done", False)
   427→    marker = "[x]" if done else "[ ]"
   428→    title = step.get("title", "")
   429→    print(f"    {i}. {marker} {title}")
   430→    if done:
   431→        print(colorize("         (completed)", "dim"))
   432→        return
   433→    detail = step.get("detail", "")
   434→    if detail:
   435→        for line in detail.splitlines():
   436→            print(colorize(f"         {line}", "dim"))
   437→    refs = step.get("issue_refs", [])
   438→    if refs:
   439→        print(colorize(f"         Refs: {', '.join(refs)}", "dim"))

   442→def _cmd_cluster_show(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   443→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   444→    plan = load_plan()

   446→    if cluster is None:

   448→        return
   449→
   450→    # Header
   451→    auto_tag = "Auto-generated" if cluster.get("auto") else "Manual"
   452→    cluster_key = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   453→    key_type = f" ({cluster_key.split('::', 1)[0]})" if cluster_key else ""
   454→    print(colorize(f"  Cluster: {cluster_name}", "bold"))
   455→    print(colorize(f"  Type: {auto_tag}{key_type}", "dim"))
   456→    priority = cluster.get("priority")
   457→    if priority is not None:
   458→        print(colorize(f"  Priority: {priority}", "dim"))
   459→    dep_order = cluster.get("dependency_order")
   460→    if dep_order is not None:

   463→    if desc:
   464→        print(colorize(f"  Description: {desc}", "dim"))

   466→    if action:

   471→    if steps:
   472→        done_count = sum(1 for s in steps if isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("done", False))
   473→        print()

   475→        print(colorize(f"  Steps ({len(steps)}){suffix}:", "dim"))
   476→        for i, step in enumerate(steps, 1):

   486→        print(colorize(f"  Members ({len(issue_ids)}):", "dim"))

   494→    print(colorize(f"    Drill in:     desloppify next --cluster {cluster_name} --count 10", "dim"))
   495→    print(colorize(f"    Skip:         desloppify plan skip {cluster_name}", "dim"))

   498→def _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(
   499→    clusters: dict, queue_order: list[str],
   500→) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, dict]], dict[str, int]]:
   501→    """Sort clusters by (priority, earliest queue position).
   502→
   503→    Clusters with explicit priority sort first (ascending), then unset-priority
   504→    clusters sort by queue position.
   505→
   506→    Returns (sorted_cluster_pairs, min_pos_cache) where min_pos_cache maps
   507→    cluster name to its earliest queue position (999_999 if no members queued).
   508→    """
   509→    pos_map = {fid: i for i, fid in enumerate(queue_order)}
   510→
   511→    def _min_pos(cluster_data: dict) -> int:
   512→        positions = [pos_map[fid] for fid in cluster_data.get("issue_ids", []) if fid in pos_map]
   513→        return min(positions) if positions else 999_999
   514→
   515→    min_pos_cache = {name: _min_pos(c) for name, c in clusters.items()}
   516→    sorted_clusters = sorted(
   517→        clusters.items(),
   518→        key=lambda kv: (kv[1].get("priority", 999), min_pos_cache[kv[0]]),
   519→    )
   520→    return sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache
   521→
   522→
   523→def _print_cluster_list_verbose(
   524→    sorted_clusters: list[tuple[str, dict]],
   525→    min_pos_cache: dict[str, int],
   526→    active: str | None,
   527→) -> None:
   528→    """Print the verbose table view of the cluster list."""
   529→    name_width = max(20, min(35, max(len(n) for n, _ in sorted_clusters)))
   530→    total = len(sorted_clusters)
   531→    has_dep = any(c.get("dependency_order") is not None for _, c in sorted_clusters)
   532→    print(colorize(f"  Clusters ({total} total, sorted by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   533→    print()
   534→    dep_header = f"  {'Dep':>3}" if has_dep else ""
   535→    header = f"  {'#pos':<5}  {'Pri':>3}{dep_header}  {'Name':<{name_width}}  {'Items':>5}  {'Steps':>5}  {'Type':<6}  Description"
   536→    dep_sep = f"  {'─'*3}" if has_dep else ""
   537→    sep = f"  {'─'*4}  {'─'*3}{dep_sep}  {'─'*name_width}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*5}  {'─'*6}  {'─'*40}"
   538→    print(colorize(header, "dim"))
   539→    print(colorize(sep, "dim"))
   540→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   541→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   542→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   543→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   544→        pri_str = str(priority) if priority is not None else "—"
   545→        dep_order = cluster.get("dependency_order")
   546→        dep_str = f"  {dep_order:>3}" if has_dep and dep_order is not None else ("  {:>3}".format("—") if has_dep else "")
   547→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   548→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
   549→        steps_str = str(len(steps)) if steps else "—"
   550→        type_str = "auto" if cluster.get("auto") else "manual"
   551→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   552→        if not desc and min_p == 999_999 and not member_count:
   553→            desc = "(no queue position — no members)"
   554→        desc_truncated = (desc[:39] + "…") if len(desc) > 40 else desc
   555→        name_display = (name[:name_width - 1] + "…") if len(name) > name_width else name
   556→        focused = " *" if name == active else ""
   557→        print(f"  {pos_str:>5}  {pri_str:>3}{dep_str}  {name_display:<{name_width}}  {member_count:>5}  {steps_str:>5}  {type_str:<6}  {desc_truncated}{focused}")
   558→    print()
   559→
   560→
   561→def _cmd_cluster_list(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   562→    plan = load_plan()
   563→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   564→    active = plan.get("active_cluster")
   565→    verbose: bool = getattr(args, "verbose", False)
   566→    missing_steps: bool = getattr(args, "missing_steps", False)
   567→
   568→    if not clusters:
   569→        print("  No clusters defined.")
   570→        return
   571→
   572→    queue_order: list[str] = plan.get("queue_order", [])
   573→    sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache = _sorted_clusters_by_queue_pos(clusters, queue_order)
   574→
   575→    if missing_steps:
   576→        from desloppify.app.commands.plan.triage.stage_helpers import _unenriched_clusters
   577→        gaps = _unenriched_clusters(plan)
   578→        if not gaps:
   579→            print(colorize("  All clusters have action steps.", "green"))
   580→            return
   581→        print(colorize(f"  {len(gaps)} cluster(s) need action steps:", "bold"))
   582→        for name, missing in gaps:
   583→            print(colorize(f"    {name}: missing {', '.join(missing)}", "yellow"))
   584→        print()
   585→        print(colorize("  Fix with:", "dim"))
   586→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --description "..." --steps "step1" "step2"', "dim"))
   587→        print(colorize('    desloppify plan cluster update <name> --add-step "step title" --detail "sub-details"', "dim"))
   588→        return
   589→
   590→    if verbose:
   591→        _print_cluster_list_verbose(sorted_clusters, min_pos_cache, active)
   592→        return
   593→
   594→    print(colorize("  Clusters (ordered by priority/queue position):", "bold"))
   595→    for name, cluster in sorted_clusters:
   596→        min_p = min_pos_cache[name]
   597→        pos_str = f"#{min_p}" if min_p < 999_999 else "—"
   598→        priority = cluster.get("priority")
   599→        pri_tag = f" [P{priority}]" if priority is not None else ""
   600→        member_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   601→        desc = cluster.get("description") or ""
   602→        marker = " (focused)" if name == active else ""
   603→        desc_str = f" — {desc}" if desc else ""
   604→        auto_tag = " [auto]" if cluster.get("auto") else ""
   605→        print(f"    {pos_str:>5} {pri_tag} {name}: {member_count} items{auto_tag}{desc_str}{marker}")
   606→

   608→def _cmd_cluster_update(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   609→    """Update cluster description, steps, and/or priority."""
   610→    cluster_name: str = getattr(args, "cluster_name", "")
   611→    description: str | None = getattr(args, "description", None)
   612→    steps: list[str] | None = getattr(args, "steps", None)
   613→    steps_file: str | None = getattr(args, "steps_file", None)
   614→    add_step: str | None = getattr(args, "add_step", None)
   615→    detail: str | None = getattr(args, "detail", None)
   616→    update_step: int | None = getattr(args, "update_step", None)
   617→    remove_step: int | None = getattr(args, "remove_step", None)
   618→    done_step: int | None = getattr(args, "done_step", None)
   619→    undone_step: int | None = getattr(args, "undone_step", None)
   620→    priority: int | None = getattr(args, "priority", None)
   621→    effort: str | None = getattr(args, "effort", None)

   809→
   810→def _cmd_cluster_import(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   811→    """Bulk create/update clusters from a YAML file."""
   812→    file_path: str = getattr(args, "file", "")
   813→    dry_run: bool = getattr(args, "dry_run", False)
   814→
   815→    path = Path(file_path)
   816→    if not path.is_file():
   817→        print(colorize(f"  File not found: {file_path}", "red"))
   818→        return
   819→
   820→    import yaml  # noqa: PLC0415
   821→    data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
   822→    if not isinstance(data, dict) or "clusters" not in data:
   823→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: expected top-level 'clusters' key.", "red"))
   824→        return
   825→
   826→    entries = data["clusters"]
   827→    if not isinstance(entries, list):
   828→        print(colorize("  Invalid YAML: 'clusters' must be a list.", "red"))
   829→        return
   830→
   831→    plan = load_plan()
   832→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   833→    created = 0
   834→    updated = 0
   835→
   836→    for entry in entries:
   837→        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "name" not in entry:
   838→            print(colorize(f"  Skipping entry without 'name': {entry!r}", "yellow"))
   839→            continue
   840→        name = entry["name"]
   841→        is_new = name not in clusters
   842→
   843→        if dry_run:
   844→            action = "CREATE" if is_new else "UPDATE"
   845→            step_count = len(entry.get("steps", []))
   846→            print(colorize(f"  [{action}] {name}: {step_count} step(s)", "cyan"))
   847→            continue
   848→
   849→        if is_new:
   850→            try:
   851→                cluster = create_cluster(plan, name, entry.get("description"))
   852→            except ValueError as ex:
   853→                print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   854→                continue
   855→            created += 1
   856→        else:
   857→            cluster = clusters[name]
   858→            updated += 1
   859→
   860→        if "description" in entry:
   861→            cluster["description"] = entry["description"]
   862→        if "priority" in entry:
   863→            cluster["priority"] = entry["priority"]
   864→        if "steps" in entry:
   865→            imported_steps = []
   866→            for s in entry["steps"]:
   867→                if isinstance(s, str):
   868→                    imported_steps.append({"title": s})
   869→                elif isinstance(s, dict):
   870→                    step: dict = {"title": s.get("title", "")}
   871→                    if "detail" in s:
   872→                        step["detail"] = s["detail"]
   873→                    if "refs" in s:
   874→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["refs"]
   875→                    elif "issue_refs" in s:
   876→                        step["issue_refs"] = s["issue_refs"]
   877→                    imported_steps.append(step)
   878→            cluster["action_steps"] = imported_steps
   879→        cluster["user_modified"] = True
   880→        cluster["updated_at"] = utc_now()
   881→
   882→    if dry_run:
   883→        print(colorize("  (dry run — no changes saved)", "dim"))
   884→        return
   885→
   886→    save_plan(plan)
   887→    print(colorize(f"  Import complete: {created} created, {updated} updated.", "green"))
   888→
   889→
   890→def _cmd_cluster_merge(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   891→    """Merge source cluster into target cluster."""
   892→    source: str = getattr(args, "source", "")
   893→    target: str = getattr(args, "target", "")
   894→
   895→    plan = load_plan()
   896→    try:
   897→        added, source_ids = merge_clusters(plan, source, target)
   898→    except ValueError as ex:
   899→        print(colorize(f"  {ex}", "red"))
   900→        return
   901→
   902→    append_log_entry(
   903→        plan, "cluster_merge", issue_ids=source_ids,
   904→        cluster_name=target, actor="user",
   905→        detail={"source": source, "added": added},
   906→    )
   907→    save_plan(plan)
   908→    print(colorize(
   909→        f"  Merged cluster {source!r} into {target!r}: "
   910→        f"{added} issue(s) added, {len(source_ids)} total moved. Source deleted.",
   911→        "green",
   912→    ))
   913→
   914→
   915→def cmd_cluster_dispatch(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   916→    """Route cluster subcommands."""
   917→    cluster_action = getattr(args, "cluster_action", None)
   918→    dispatch = {
   919→        "create": _cmd_cluster_create,
   920→        "add": _cmd_cluster_add,
   921→        "remove": _cmd_cluster_remove,
   922→        "delete": _cmd_cluster_delete,
   923→        "reorder": _cmd_cluster_reorder,
   924→        "show": _cmd_cluster_show,
   925→        "list": _cmd_cluster_list,
   926→        "update": _cmd_cluster_update,
   927→        "merge": _cmd_cluster_merge,
   928→        "export": _cmd_cluster_export,
   929→        "import": _cmd_cluster_import,
   930→    }
   931→    handler = dispatch.get(cluster_action)
   932→    if handler is None:
   933→        _cmd_cluster_list(args)

   935→    handler(args)

     3→Classifies files into zones (production, test, config, generated, script, vendor)

    25→class Zone(str, Enum):
    26→    """File intent zone — determines scoring and detection policy."""
    27→
    28→    PRODUCTION = "production"

    32→    SCRIPT = "script"
    33→    VENDOR = "vendor"

    35→
    36→# Zones excluded from the health score

    43→@dataclass
    44→class ZoneRule:
    45→    """A classification rule: zone + list of path patterns.
    46→
    47→    Patterns are matched against relative file paths. First matching rule wins.
    48→    Pattern types (auto-detected from shape):
    49→      - "/dir/"   → substring match on full path (directory marker)
    50→      - ".ext"    → basename ends-with (suffix/extension, e.g. ".d.ts", ".test.")
    51→      - "prefix_" → basename starts-with (trailing underscore)
    52→      - "name.py" → basename exact match (has extension, no /)
    53→      - fallback  → substring on full path
    54→    """
    55→
    56→    zone: Zone
    57→    patterns: list[str]
    58→
    59→
    60→def _match_pattern(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match a zone pattern against a relative file path.
    62→
    63→    See ZoneRule docstring for pattern type conventions.
    64→    """
    65→    basename = os.path.basename(rel_path)
    66→
    67→    # Directory pattern: "/dir/" → substring on padded path
    68→    if pattern.startswith("/") and pattern.endswith("/"):
    69→        return pattern in ("/" + rel_path + "/")
    70→
    71→    # Suffix/extension pattern: starts with "." → contains on basename
    72→    if pattern.startswith("."):
    73→        return pattern in basename
    74→
    75→    # Prefix pattern: ends with "_" → basename starts-with
    76→    if pattern.endswith("_"):
    77→        return basename.startswith(pattern)
    78→
    79→    # Suffix pattern: starts with "_" → basename ends-with (_test.py, _pb2.py)
    80→    if pattern.startswith("_"):
    81→        return basename.endswith(pattern)
    82→
    83→    # Exact basename: has a proper file extension (1-5 chars after last dot),
    84→    # no "/" → exact basename match (config.py, setup.py, conftest.py)
    85→    if "/" not in pattern and "." in pattern:
    86→        ext = pattern.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    87→        if ext and len(ext) <= 5 and ext.isalnum():
    88→            return basename == pattern
    89→
    90→    # Fallback: substring on full path (vite.config, tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
    91→    return pattern in rel_path
    92→
    93→

    95→
    96→COMMON_ZONE_RULES = [
    97→    ZoneRule(Zone.VENDOR, ["/vendor/", "/third_party/", "/vendored/"]),
    98→    ZoneRule(Zone.GENERATED, ["/generated/", "/__generated__/"]),
    99→    ZoneRule(Zone.TEST, ["/tests/", "/test/", "/fixtures/"]),
   100→    ZoneRule(Zone.SCRIPT, ["/scripts/", "/bin/"]),
   101→]

   103→
   104→def classify_file(
   105→    rel_path: str, rules: list[ZoneRule], overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
   106→) -> Zone:
   107→    """Classify a file by its relative path. Overrides take priority."""
   108→    if overrides:
   109→        override = overrides.get(rel_path)
   110→        if override:
   111→            try:
   112→                return Zone(override)
   113→            except ValueError as exc:
   114→                log_best_effort_failure(
   115→                    logger, f"parse zone override for {rel_path}", exc
   116→                )
   117→    for rule in rules:
   118→        for pattern in rule.patterns:
   119→            if _match_pattern(rel_path, pattern):
   120→                return rule.zone
   121→    return Zone.PRODUCTION

   124→class FileZoneMap:
   125→    """Cached zone classification for a set of files.
   126→
   127→    Built once per scan from file list + zone rules.
   128→    """
   129→
   130→    def __init__(
   131→        self,
   132→        files: list[str],
   133→        rules: list[ZoneRule],
   134→        rel_fn=None,
   135→        overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   136→    ):
   137→        """Build a zone map from files, ordered rules, and optional overrides."""
   138→        self._map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   139→        self._overrides = overrides
   140→        for f in files:
   141→            rp = rel_fn(f) if rel_fn else f
   142→            self._map[f] = classify_file(rp, rules, overrides)
   143→
   144→    def get(self, path: str) -> Zone:
   145→        """Get zone for a file path. Returns PRODUCTION if not classified."""
   146→        return self._map.get(path, Zone.PRODUCTION)
   147→
   148→    def exclude(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   149→        """Return files NOT in the given zones."""
   150→        zone_set = set(zones)
   151→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) not in zone_set]
   152→
   153→    def include_only(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   154→        """Return files that ARE in the given zones."""
   155→        zone_set = set(zones)
   156→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) in zone_set]
   157→
   158→    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   159→        """Return file count per zone."""
   160→        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   161→        for zone in self._map.values():
   162→            counts[zone.value] = counts.get(zone.value, 0) + 1
   163→        return counts
   164→
   165→    def production_count(self) -> int:
   166→        """Count files classified as production."""
   167→        return len(self._map) - self.non_production_count()
   168→
   169→    def non_production_count(self) -> int:
   170→        """Count files in excluded zones (test/config/generated/vendor)."""
   171→        return sum(1 for z in self._map.values() if z in EXCLUDED_ZONES)
   172→
   173→    def all_files(self) -> list[str]:
   174→        """Return all classified file paths."""
   175→        return list(self._map.keys())
   176→
   177→    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Zone]]:
   178→        """Return all (path, zone) pairs."""
   179→        return list(self._map.items())

   207→        skip_detectors=CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   208→        exclude_from_score=True,
   209→    ),
   210→    Zone.GENERATED: ZonePolicy(
   211→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   212→        exclude_from_score=True,
   213→    ),
   214→    Zone.VENDOR: ZonePolicy(
   215→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   216→        exclude_from_score=True,
   217→    ),
   218→    Zone.SCRIPT: ZonePolicy(
   219→        skip_detectors=SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   220→        downgrade_detectors={"structural"},
   221→    ),
   222→}
   223→
   224→
   225→# ── Helpers for phase runners ─────────────────────────────
   226→
   227→
   228→def adjust_potential(zone_map, total: int) -> int:
   229→    """Subtract non-production files from a potential count.
   230→
   231→    Uses the zone map's own file list — no need to pass files separately.
   232→    No-op if zone_map is None.
   233→    """
   234→    if zone_map is None:
   235→        return total
   236→    return max(total - zone_map.non_production_count(), 0)
   237→
   238→
   239→def should_skip_issue(zone_map, filepath: str, detector: str) -> bool:
   240→    """Check if a issue should be skipped based on zone policy.
   241→
   242→    Returns True if the file's zone policy says to skip this detector.
   243→    """
   244→    if zone_map is None:
   245→        return False
   246→    zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   247→    policy = ZONE_POLICIES.get(zone)
   248→    return policy is not None and detector in policy.skip_detectors
   249→
   250→
   251→def filter_entries(
   252→    zone_map, entries: list[dict], detector: str, file_key: str = "file"
   253→) -> list[dict]:
   254→    """Filter detector entries by zone policy. No-op if zone_map is None.
   255→
   256→    If file_key points to a list (e.g. cycle entries with "files"), checks
   257→    the first element.
   258→    """
   259→    if zone_map is None:
   260→        return entries
   261→
   262→    def _get_path(entry):
   263→        val = entry[file_key]
   264→        return val[0] if isinstance(val, list) else val
   265→
   266→    return [
   267→        e for e in entries if not should_skip_issue(zone_map, _get_path(e), detector)
   268→    ]
   269→

    97→def _save_plan_state_transactional(
    98→    *,
    99→    plan: dict,
   100→    plan_path: Path | None,
   101→    state_data: dict,
   102→    state_path_value: Path | None,
   103→) -> None:
   104→    """Persist plan+state together; rollback both files on partial write failure."""
   105→    effective_plan_path = _resolve_plan_file(plan_path)
   106→    effective_state_path = _resolve_state_file(state_path_value)
   107→    plan_snapshot = _snapshot_file(effective_plan_path)
   108→    state_snapshot = _snapshot_file(effective_state_path)
   109→
   110→    try:
   111→        state_mod.save_state(state_data, effective_state_path)
   112→        save_plan(plan, effective_plan_path)
   113→    except Exception:
   114→        _restore_file_snapshot(effective_state_path, state_snapshot)
   115→        _restore_file_snapshot(effective_plan_path, plan_snapshot)
   116→        raise

   225→    if not require_completed_scan(state):

   228→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])

   233→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   234→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   235→
   236→    kind = skip_kind_from_flags(permanent=permanent, false_positive=false_positive)
   237→    if not _validate_skip_requirements(
   238→        kind=kind,
   239→        attestation=attestation,
   240→        note=note,

   244→    state_file = runtime.state_path
   245→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)

   248→    if not issue_ids:

   252→    # Bulk skip guard — prevent agents from draining the queue in one shot
   253→    if len(issue_ids) > _BULK_SKIP_THRESHOLD:

   373→def cmd_plan_reopen(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   374→    """Reopen resolved issues from plan context."""
   375→    patterns: list[str] = getattr(args, "patterns", [])
   376→
   377→    raw_state_path = state_path(args)
   378→    state_file = raw_state_path if isinstance(raw_state_path, Path) else Path(raw_state_path) if raw_state_path else None
   379→    state_data = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   380→    plan_file = _plan_file_for_state(state_file)
   381→
   382→    reopened: list[str] = []
   383→    for pattern in patterns:
   384→        reopened.extend(
   385→            state_mod.resolve_issues(state_data, pattern, "open")
   386→        )
   387→
   388→    if not reopened:
   389→        print(colorize("  No resolved issues matching: " + " ".join(patterns), "yellow"))
   390→        return
   391→
   392→    # Remove from skipped if present, and ensure all reopened IDs are in queue
   393→    plan = load_plan(plan_file)
   394→
   395→    # Remove from commit tracking uncommitted list
   396→    purge_uncommitted_ids(plan, reopened)
   397→
   398→    skipped = plan.get("skipped", {})
   399→    count = 0
   400→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   401→    for fid in reopened:
   402→        if fid in skipped:
   403→            skipped.pop(fid)
   404→            count += 1
   405→        if fid not in order:
   406→            plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   407→            order.add(fid)
   408→            count += 1
   409→    append_log_entry(
   410→        plan, "reopen", issue_ids=reopened, actor="user",
   411→    )
   412→    _save_plan_state_transactional(
   413→        plan=plan,
   414→        plan_path=plan_file,
   415→        state_data=state_data,
   416→        state_path_value=state_file,
   417→    )
   418→
   419→    print(colorize(f"  Reopened {len(reopened)} issue(s).", "green"))
   420→    if count:
   421→        print(colorize("  Plan updated: items moved back to queue.", "dim"))

   427→def _check_cluster_guard(patterns: list[str], plan: dict, state: dict) -> bool:
   428→    """Return True if blocked by cluster guard, False if OK to proceed."""
   429→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   430→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   431→    for pattern in patterns:
   432→        if pattern in clusters:
   433→            cluster = clusters[pattern]
   434→            # Filter to alive issues only — stale IDs should not count
   435→            ids = [
   436→                fid for fid in cluster.get("issue_ids", [])
   437→                if fid in issues and issues[fid].get("status") == "open"
   438→            ]
   439→            if len(ids) == 0:
   440→                print(colorize(
   441→                    f"\n  Cluster '{pattern}' is empty — add items before marking it done.\n",
   442→                    "yellow",
   443→                ))
   444→                print(colorize(
   445→                    f"  Use: desloppify plan cluster add {pattern} <issue-id>",
   446→                    "dim",
   447→                ))
   448→                return True  # blocked
   449→            if len(ids) <= _CLUSTER_INDIVIDUAL_THRESHOLD:
   450→                _print_cluster_guard(pattern, ids, state)
   451→                return True  # blocked
   452→    return False  # OK
   453→

   455→def _print_cluster_guard(cluster_name: str, issue_ids: list[str], state: dict) -> None:
   456→    issues = state.get("issues", {})
   457→    print(colorize(
   458→        f"\n  Cluster '{cluster_name}' has {len(issue_ids)} item(s) — mark them done individually first:\n",
   459→        "yellow",
   460→    ))
   461→    for fid in issue_ids:
   462→        f = issues.get(fid, {})
   463→        summary = f.get("summary", "(no summary)")[:80]
   464→        detector = f.get("detector", "?")
   465→        print(f"    {fid}  [{detector}]  {summary}")
   466→    print(colorize(
   467→        "\n  Use: desloppify resolve <id> --status fixed --note '...' --attest '...'",
   468→        "dim",

   470→    print(colorize(
   471→        "  Or mark each resolved: desloppify plan resolve <id> --note '...' --confirm\n",
   472→        "dim",

   476→def _is_synthetic_id(fid: str) -> bool:
   477→    """Return True if the ID is a synthetic workflow/triage item, not a real issue."""
   478→    return fid.startswith("triage::") or fid.startswith("workflow::") or fid.startswith("subjective::")
   479→
   480→
   481→def _resolve_synthetic_ids(patterns: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
   482→    """Separate synthetic IDs from real issue patterns.
   483→
   484→    Returns (synthetic_ids, remaining_patterns).
   485→    """
   486→    synthetic = [p for p in patterns if _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   487→    remaining = [p for p in patterns if not _is_synthetic_id(p)]
   488→    return synthetic, remaining
   489→

   491→def _blocked_triage_stages(plan: dict) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
   492→    """Return ``{stage_id: [blocked_by_ids]}`` for triage stages that can't run yet.
   493→
   494→    Uses the dependency graph and confirmed-stage metadata directly —
   495→    no state needed, no queue item construction.
   496→    """
   497→    order_set = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
   498→    present = order_set & TRIAGE_IDS
   499→    if not present:
   500→        return {}
   501→
   502→    confirmed = set(plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {}).get("triage_stages", {}).keys())
   503→    stage_names = ("observe", "reflect", "organize", "enrich", "commit")
   504→
   505→    blocked: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   506→    for sid, name in zip(TRIAGE_STAGE_IDS, stage_names, strict=False):
   507→        if sid not in present or name in confirmed:
   508→            continue
   509→        deps = TRIAGE_STAGE_DEPENDENCIES.get(name, set())
   510→        unmet = sorted(
   511→            f"triage::{dep}" for dep in deps
   512→            if f"triage::{dep}" in present and dep not in confirmed
   513→        )
   514→        if unmet:
   515→            blocked[sid] = unmet
   516→    return blocked
   517→

   519→def cmd_plan_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   520→    """Mark issues as fixed — delegates to cmd_resolve for rich UX."""

   810→def cmd_plan_scan_gate(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   811→    """Check or skip the scan requirement for workflow items."""
   812→    skip = getattr(args, "skip", False)
   813→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   814→
   815→    plan = load_plan()
   816→    scan_count_at_start = plan.get("scan_count_at_plan_start")
   817→
   818→    if scan_count_at_start is None:
   819→        print(colorize("  No active plan cycle (plan_start_scores not seeded).", "dim"))
   820→        print(colorize("  Scan gate is not applicable — workflow items gate themselves.", "dim"))
   821→        return
   822→
   823→    resolved_state_path = state_path(args)
   824→    state_data = state_mod.load_state(resolved_state_path)
   825→    current_scan_count = int(state_data.get("scan_count", 0) or 0)
   826→    scan_ran = current_scan_count > scan_count_at_start
   827→    scan_skipped = plan.get("scan_gate_skipped", False)
   828→
   829→    if not skip:
   830→        # Status check
   831→        if scan_ran:
   832→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: PASSED", "green"))
   833→            print(colorize(
   834→                f"  Scans at cycle start: {scan_count_at_start}  "
   835→                f"Current: {current_scan_count}",
   836→                "dim",
   837→            ))
   838→        elif scan_skipped:
   839→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: SKIPPED (manually)", "yellow"))
   840→        else:
   841→            print(colorize("  Scan gate: BLOCKED", "red"))
   842→            print(colorize(

   847→            print(colorize("  Run: desloppify scan", "dim"))
   848→            print(colorize(
   849→                '  Or:  desloppify plan scan-gate --skip --note "reason"',
   850→                "dim",
   851→            ))
   852→        return
   853→
   854→    # --skip mode
   855→    if scan_ran:
   856→        print(colorize("  Scan already ran this cycle — no skip needed.", "green"))
   857→        return
   858→
   859→    if not note or len(note.strip()) < 50:
   860→        print(colorize(

   862→            "red",
   863→        ))
   864→        return

    31→def _detect_unreachable_code(
    32→    filepath: str,
    33→    tree: ast.Module,
    34→    *,
    35→    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
    36→) -> list[dict]:
    37→    """Flag statements after unconditional return/raise/break/continue.
    38→
    39→    Walks every statement block (function body, if/else body, etc.) and flags
    40→    any statement that follows an unconditional flow-control statement.
    41→    """
    42→    _TERMINAL = (ast.Return, ast.Raise, ast.Break, ast.Continue)
    43→    results: list[dict] = []
    44→
    45→    def _check_block(stmts: list[ast.stmt]):
    46→        for i, stmt in enumerate(stmts):
    47→            if isinstance(stmt, _TERMINAL) and i < len(stmts) - 1:
    48→                next_stmt = stmts[i + 1]
    49→                # Skip flagging string constants (often used as section markers)
    50→                if isinstance(next_stmt, ast.Expr) and isinstance(
    51→                    next_stmt.value, ast.Constant
    52→                ):
    53→                    continue
    54→                results.append(
    55→                    {
    56→                        "file": filepath,
    57→                        "line": next_stmt.lineno,
    58→                        "content": f"unreachable after {type(stmt).__name__.lower()} on line {stmt.lineno}",
    59→                    }
    60→                )
    61→            # Recurse into compound statements
    62→            for attr in ("body", "orelse", "finalbody", "handlers"):
    63→                block = getattr(stmt, attr, None)
    64→                if isinstance(block, list):
    65→                    child_stmts = [s for s in block if isinstance(s, ast.stmt)]
    66→                    if child_stmts:
    67→                        _check_block(child_stmts)
    68→            # ExceptHandler has a body too
    69→            if isinstance(stmt, ast.ExceptHandler):
    70→                _check_block(stmt.body)
    71→
    72→    for node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
    73→        _check_block(node.body)
    74→    return results
    75→
    76→
    77→def _detect_constant_return(
    78→    filepath: str,
    79→    tree: ast.Module,
    80→    *,
    81→    all_nodes: tuple[ast.AST, ...] | None = None,
    82→) -> list[dict]:
    83→    """Flag functions that always return the same constant value.
    84→
    85→    Analyzes all return paths — if every return statement returns the same
    86→    literal value (True, False, None, a number, or a string), the function
    87→    likely has dead logic or is a stub masquerading as real code.
    88→    """
    89→    results: list[dict] = []
    90→    for node in _iter_nodes(tree, all_nodes, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
    91→        # Skip tiny functions (stubs/pass-only already caught by dead_function)
    92→        if not hasattr(node, "end_lineno") or not node.end_lineno:
    93→            continue
    94→        loc = node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1
    95→        if loc < 4:
    96→            continue
    97→        # Skip decorated functions (properties, abstractmethods, etc.)
    98→        if node.decorator_list:
    99→            continue

    38→def _cmd_triage_complete(

    42→) -> None:
    43→    """Complete triage — requires organize stage (or confirm-existing path)."""
    44→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
    45→    strategy: str | None = getattr(args, "strategy", None)
    46→    attestation: str | None = getattr(args, "attestation", None)
    47→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
    48→
    49→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
    50→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to complete.", "yellow"))
    51→        return
    52→
    53→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
    54→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
    55→
    56→    state = resolved_services.command_runtime(args).state
    57→    review_ids = open_review_ids_from_state(state)
    58→
    59→    # Require organize stage confirmed

    65→        return
    66→

    72→    ):

   134→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(

   136→        "triage_complete",
   137→        actor="user",
   138→        detail={
   139→            "strategy_len": len(strategy.strip()),
   140→            "coverage": f"{organized}/{total}",
   141→        },
   142→    )
   143→
   144→    apply_completion(args, plan, strategy, services=resolved_services)
   145→
   146→    print_user_message(
   147→        "Hey — triage is done. Run `desloppify next` and start"
   148→        " executing the plan. Don't stop until you're done —"
   149→        " unless I've told you otherwise, just go."
   150→    )
   151→
   152→
   153→def _cmd_confirm_existing(
   154→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   155→    *,
   156→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   157→) -> None:
   158→    """Fast-track: confirm existing plan structure is still valid."""
   159→    resolved_services = services or default_triage_services()
   160→    note: str | None = getattr(args, "note", None)
   161→    strategy: str | None = getattr(args, "strategy", None)
   162→    confirmed: str | None = getattr(args, "confirmed", None)
   163→    plan = resolved_services.load_plan()
   164→
   165→    if not has_triage_in_queue(plan):
   166→        print(colorize("  No planning stages in the queue — nothing to confirm.", "yellow"))
   167→        return
   168→
   169→    meta = plan.get("epic_triage_meta", {})
   170→    stages = meta.get("triage_stages", {})
   171→
   172→    # Require a prior completed triage — can't skip the full flow on first run
   173→    if not _require_prior_strategy_for_confirm(meta):
   174→        return
   175→
   176→    # Determine if this is a light-path (additions only) or full ceremony
   177→    runtime = resolved_services.command_runtime(args)
   178→    state = runtime.state
   179→    si = resolved_services.collect_triage_input(plan, state)
   180→    has_only_additions = bool(si.new_since_last) and not si.resolved_since_last
   181→
   182→    if not _confirm_existing_stages_valid(
   183→        stages=stages,
   184→        has_only_additions=has_only_additions,
   185→        si=si,
   186→    ):
   187→        return
   188→
   189→    # Require existing enriched clusters
   190→    clusters_with_issues = manual_clusters_with_issues(plan)
   191→    if not clusters_with_issues:
   192→        print(colorize("  Cannot confirm existing: no clusters with issues exist.", "red"))
   193→        print(colorize("  Use the full organize flow instead.", "dim"))
   194→        return
   195→
   196→    # Require note
   197→    if not _confirm_note_valid(note):
   198→        return
   199→
   200→    # Require strategy (default to "same" on light path)
   201→    strategy = _resolve_confirm_existing_strategy(
   202→        strategy,
   203→        has_only_additions=has_only_additions,
   204→        meta=meta,
   205→    )
   206→    if strategy is None:
   207→        return
   208→
   209→    # Strategy length check (unless "same")
   210→    if not _confirm_strategy_valid(strategy):
   211→        return
   212→
   213→    # Require --confirmed with plan review
   214→    confirmed_text = _confirmed_text_or_error(
   215→        plan=plan,
   216→        state=state,
   217→        confirmed=confirmed,
   218→    )
   219→    if confirmed_text is None:
   220→        return
   221→
   222→    # Validate: note cites at least 1 new/changed issue (if there are any)
   223→    if not _note_cites_new_issues_or_error(note, si):
   224→        return
   225→
   226→    # Record organize as confirmed-existing and complete
   227→    stages = meta.setdefault("triage_stages", {})
   228→    _record_confirm_existing_completion(
   229→        stages=stages,
   230→        note=note,
   231→        issue_count=len(clusters_with_issues),
   232→        confirmed_text=confirmed_text,
   233→    )
   234→
   235→    resolved_services.append_log_entry(
   236→        plan,
   237→        "triage_confirm_existing",
   238→        actor="user",
   239→        detail={"confirmed_text": confirmed_text},
   240→    )
   241→
   242→    apply_completion(args, plan, strategy, services=resolved_services)
   243→    print(colorize("  Confirmed existing plan — triage complete.", "green"))
   244→
   245→
   246→def cmd_triage_complete(
   247→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   248→    *,
   249→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   250→) -> None:
   251→    """Public entrypoint for triage completion."""
   252→    _cmd_triage_complete(args, services=services)
   253→
   254→
   255→def cmd_confirm_existing(
   256→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   257→    *,
   258→    services: TriageServices | None = None,
   259→) -> None:
   260→    """Public entrypoint for confirm-existing completion path."""
   261→    _cmd_confirm_existing(args, services=services)
   262→
   263→
   264→__all__ = [
   265→    "cmd_confirm_existing",
   266→    "cmd_triage_complete",
   267→    "_cmd_confirm_existing",
   268→    "_cmd_triage_complete",
   269→]

1→"""Stage-gate and coverage helpers for triage command handlers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.base.output.terminal import colorize
     6→from desloppify.engine.plan import TRIAGE_IDS
     7→
     8→
     9→def _require_triage_pending(plan: dict, *, action: str) -> bool:
    10→    """Require at least one triage stage ID to be present in queue for an action."""
    11→    order = set(plan.get("queue_order", []))
    12→    if order & TRIAGE_IDS:
    13→        return True
    14→    print(colorize(f"  No triage stage in the queue — nothing to {action}.", "yellow"))
    15→    return False
    16→
    17→
    18→def _validate_stage_report(
    19→    report: str | None,
    20→    *,
    21→    stage: str,
    22→    min_chars: int,
    23→    missing_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    24→    short_guidance: list[str] | None = None,
    25→) -> str | None:
    26→    """Validate staged report presence/length and print consistent guidance."""
    27→    if not report:
    28→        print(colorize(f"  --report is required for --stage {stage}.", "red"))
    29→        for line in missing_guidance or []:
    30→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    31→        return None
    32→    cleaned = report.strip()
    33→    if len(cleaned) < min_chars:
    34→        print(
    35→            colorize(
    36→                f"  Report too short: {len(cleaned)} chars (minimum {min_chars}).",
    37→                "red",
    38→            )
    39→        )
    40→        for line in short_guidance or []:
    41→            print(colorize(f"  {line}", "dim"))
    42→        return None
    43→    return cleaned
    44→
    45→
    46→def _triage_coverage(plan: dict) -> tuple[int, int, dict]:
    47→    """Return (organized, total, clusters) for triage progress."""
    48→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    49→    all_cluster_ids: set[str] = set()
    50→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    51→        all_cluster_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    52→    queue_ids = [issue_id for issue_id in plan.get("queue_order", []) if issue_id not in TRIAGE_IDS]
    53→    organized = sum(1 for issue_id in queue_ids if issue_id in all_cluster_ids)
    54→    return organized, len(queue_ids), clusters
    55→
    56→
    57→def _unenriched_clusters(plan: dict) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:
    58→    """Return clusters with issues that are missing required enrichment.
    59→
    60→    Requirements:
    61→    - Every cluster needs a description and at least one action_step.
    62→    - Small clusters (< 5 issues) need at least 1 action step per issue,
    63→      so each item has a concrete plan. Large clusters (>= 5) just need
    64→      steps overall (cluster-level plan is sufficient).
    65→    """
    66→    gaps: list[tuple[str, list[str]]] = []
    67→    for name, cluster in plan.get("clusters", {}).items():
    68→        if not cluster.get("issue_ids"):
    69→            continue
    70→        if cluster.get("auto"):
    71→            continue
    72→        missing: list[str] = []
    73→        if not cluster.get("description"):
    74→            missing.append("description")
    75→        steps = cluster.get("action_steps") or []
    76→        issue_count = len(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
    77→        if not steps:
    78→            missing.append("action_steps")
    79→        elif issue_count < 5 and len(steps) < issue_count:
    80→            missing.append(
    81→                f"action_steps (have {len(steps)}, need >= {issue_count} for small cluster)"
    82→            )
    83→        if missing:
    84→            gaps.append((name, missing))
    85→    return gaps
    86→
    87→
    88→def _unclustered_review_issues(plan: dict, state: dict | None = None) -> list[str]:
    89→    """Return review issue IDs that aren't in any manual cluster.
    90→
    91→    When *state* is provided, uses open review/concerns issues from state
    92→    (the canonical source). Falls back to scanning queue_order for backwards
    93→    compatibility.
    94→    """
    95→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
    96→    clustered_ids: set[str] = set()
    97→    for cluster in clusters.values():
    98→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
    99→            clustered_ids.update(cluster.get("issue_ids", []))
   100→
   101→    if state is not None:
   102→        review_ids = [
   103→            fid for fid, f in state.get("issues", {}).items()
   104→            if f.get("status") == "open" and f.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   105→        ]
   106→    else:
   107→        review_ids = [
   108→            fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   109→            if not fid.startswith("triage::") and not fid.startswith("workflow::")
   110→            and (fid.startswith("review::") or fid.startswith("concerns::"))
   111→        ]
   112→
   113→    return [fid for fid in review_ids if fid not in clustered_ids]
   114→

    57→class ClusterContext(NamedTuple):

    62→
    63→def _capture_cluster_context(
    64→    plan: dict, resolved_ids: list[str],
    65→) -> ClusterContext:
    66→    """Determine cluster membership for resolved issues, pre-purge."""
    67→    clusters = plan.get("clusters") or {}
    68→    overrides = plan.get("overrides") or {}
    69→    # Find the cluster the first resolved issue belongs to
    70→    cluster_name: str | None = None
    71→    for rid in resolved_ids:
    72→        ov = overrides.get(rid)
    73→        if ov and ov.get("cluster"):
    74→            cluster_name = ov["cluster"]
    75→            break
    76→    if not cluster_name or cluster_name not in clusters:
    77→        return ClusterContext(cluster_name=None, cluster_completed=False, cluster_remaining=0)
    78→    # Count how many will remain after these ids are removed
    79→    current_ids = set(clusters[cluster_name].get("issue_ids") or [])
    80→    remaining = current_ids - set(resolved_ids)
    81→    return ClusterContext(
    82→        cluster_name=cluster_name,
    83→        cluster_completed=len(remaining) == 0,
    84→        cluster_remaining=len(remaining),
    85→    )
    86→

    88→def _validate_fixed_note(args: argparse.Namespace) -> bool:
    89→    if args.status != "fixed":
    90→        return True
    91→    note = getattr(args, "note", None)
    92→    if validate_note_length(note):
    93→        return True
    94→    show_note_length_requirement(note)
    95→    return False
    96→

    98→def _update_living_plan_after_resolve(
    99→    *,
   100→    args: argparse.Namespace,
   101→    all_resolved: list[str],
   102→    attestation: str | None,
   103→) -> tuple[dict | None, ClusterContext]:
   104→    plan = None
   105→    ctx = ClusterContext(cluster_name=None, cluster_completed=False, cluster_remaining=0)
   106→    try:
   107→        if not has_living_plan():
   108→            return None, ctx
   109→        plan = load_plan()
   110→        ctx = _capture_cluster_context(plan, all_resolved)
   111→        purged = purge_ids(plan, all_resolved)
   112→        # Auto-complete steps whose issue_refs are all resolved
   113→        step_messages = auto_complete_steps(plan)
   114→        for msg in step_messages:
   115→            print(colorize(msg, "green"))
   116→        append_log_entry(
   117→            plan,
   118→            "resolve",
   119→            issue_ids=all_resolved,
   120→            actor="user",
   121→            note=getattr(args, "note", None),
   122→            detail={"status": args.status, "attestation": attestation},
   123→        )
   124→        if ctx.cluster_completed and ctx.cluster_name:
   125→            append_log_entry(
   126→                plan,
   127→                "cluster_done",
   128→                issue_ids=all_resolved,
   129→                cluster_name=ctx.cluster_name,
   130→                actor="user",
   131→            )
   132→        # Commit tracking: add to uncommitted on fix, remove on reopen
   133→        if args.status == "fixed":
   134→            add_uncommitted_issues(plan, all_resolved)
   135→        elif args.status == "open":
   136→            purge_uncommitted_ids(plan, all_resolved)
   137→        save_plan(plan)
   138→        if purged:
   139→            print(colorize(f"  Plan updated: {purged} item(s) removed from queue.", "dim"))
   140→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
   141→        _logger.debug("plan update failed after resolve", exc_info=True)
   142→        print(colorize("  Warning: could not update living plan.", "yellow"), file=sys.stderr)
   143→    return plan, ctx

   146→def cmd_resolve(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
   147→    """Resolve issue(s) matching one or more patterns."""
   148→    attestation = getattr(args, "attest", None)
   149→    _validate_resolve_inputs(args, attestation)
   150→    if not _validate_fixed_note(args):
   151→        return
   152→
   153→    state_file = state_path(args)
   154→    state = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
   155→
   156→    if _check_queue_order_guard(state, args.patterns, args.status):
   157→        return
   158→
   159→    if args.status == "fixed":
   160→        require_triage_current_or_exit(
   161→            state=state,
   162→            bypass=bool(getattr(args, "force_resolve", False)),
   163→            attest=getattr(args, "attest", "") or "",
   164→        )
   165→
   166→    _enforce_batch_wontfix_confirmation(
   167→        state,
   168→        args,
   169→        attestation=attestation,
   170→        resolve_all_patterns_fn=_resolve_all_patterns,
   171→    )
   172→    prev = _previous_score_snapshot(state)
   173→    prev_subjective_scores = {
   174→        str(dim): (coerce_assessment_score(payload) or 0.0)
   175→        for dim, payload in (state.get("subjective_assessments") or {}).items()
   176→        if isinstance(dim, str)
   177→    }
   178→
   179→    all_resolved = _resolve_all_patterns(state, args, attestation=attestation)
   180→    if not all_resolved:
   181→        status_label = "resolved" if args.status == "open" else "open"
   182→        print(colorize(f"No {status_label} issues matching: {' '.join(args.patterns)}", "yellow"))
   183→        return
   184→
   185→    save_state_or_exit(state, state_file)
   186→
   187→    plan, cluster_ctx = _update_living_plan_after_resolve(
   188→        args=args,
   189→        all_resolved=all_resolved,
   190→        attestation=attestation,
   191→    )
   192→    mid_cluster = (
   193→        cluster_ctx.cluster_name is not None and not cluster_ctx.cluster_completed
   194→    )
   195→
   196→    _print_resolve_summary(status=args.status, all_resolved=all_resolved)
   197→    _print_wontfix_batch_warning(
   198→        state,
   199→        status=args.status,
   200→        resolved_count=len(all_resolved),
   201→    )
   202→    show_score_with_plan_context(state, prev)
   203→    if not mid_cluster:
   204→        render_commit_guidance(state, plan, all_resolved, args.status)
   205→    _print_subjective_reset_hint(
   206→        args=args,
   207→        state=state,
   208→        all_resolved=all_resolved,
   209→        prev_subjective_scores=prev_subjective_scores,
   210→    )
   211→
   212→    lang = resolve_lang(args)
   213→    lang_name = lang.name if lang else None
   214→    narrative = narrative_mod.compute_narrative(
   215→        state,
   216→        context=narrative_mod.NarrativeContext(lang=lang_name, command="resolve"),
   217→    )
   218→    if narrative.get("milestone"):
   219→        print(colorize(f"  → {narrative['milestone']}", "green"))
   220→
   221→    next_command = _print_next_command(state)
   222→    _write_resolve_query_entry(
   223→        ResolveQueryContext(

   227→            next_command=next_command,

   232→            attestation=attestation,
